Lat. cubus , a cube: a cubical die, marked on all 6 sides (whereas the ἀστράγαλος was marked only on four sides), in plural , dice , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; the Greeks threw with three dice, so that τρὶς ἕξ, three sixes, was the highest throw, (Aeschulus Tragicus); κρίνειν τι ἐν κύβοις to decide it by the dice , by chance , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. also of the single pips on the dice , βέβληκ᾽ Ἀχιλλεὺς δύο κύβω καὶ τέσσαρα he has thrown two aces and a four, (Aeschulus Tragicus) quoted in (Aristophanes Comicus) 3. a cubic number , i. e. a number multiplied twice into itself, as 27 is the cube of 3, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

κυδοιμος.definition: the din of battle, uproar, hubbub , (Iliad by Homer) Formed from the sound. (ML)

κυδος.definition: glory, renown , especially in war, (Iliad by Homer): of a single person, κῦδος Ἀχαιῶν glory of the Achaians, like Lat. decus , (Homer) (ML)

κυκνος.definition: a swan , (Iliad by Homer), etc.:—; metaphorically , from the legends of the swan's dying song ( (Aeschulus Tragicus)), a minstrel , [ variant dates Anthology Palantina (ML)

κυμαινω.definition: 1. to rise in waves or billows, to swell , (Homer) 2. metaphorically of passion, to swell, seethe , (Pindar) 3. transitive to agitate , (Lucian) (ML)

κυνηγεω.definition: to hunt, chase , later form of κυνηγετέω, (Plutarch) (ML)

κυνικος.definition: 1. dog-like , Lat. caninus , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. Κυνικός, οῦ, a Cynic , as the followers of the philosopher Antisthenes were called, (Plutarch) (ML)

κυπαρισσινος.definition: of cypress-wood , (Odyssey by Homer) from κῦπάρισσος (ML)

κυρτος.definition: curved, arched , of a wave breaking, (Iliad by Homer); ὤμω κυρτώ round, humped , (Iliad by Homer); κ. τροχός (Euripides) (ML)

κυτος.definition: 1. the hollow of a shield or breastplate, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. any vessel, a vase, jar, urn , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.; πλεκτὸν κ. a basket, (Euripides) 3. anything that contains the body , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

κυψελη.definition: any hollow vessel: a chest, box , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

κυω.definition: 1. in present and imperfect , of females, to conceive , (Oracle quoted in Herdotus Historicus), etc. 2. rarely with accusative to be pregnant with a child, (Xenophon Historicus) 3. in aor1 ἔκυ_σα, Causal, of the male, to impregnate , and middle ἐκυ_σάμην, of the female, to conceive , (Hesiod) (ML)

κωδων.definition: a bell , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;in fortified towns an officer went round at night with a bell to challenge the sentries, and see that they were awake, (Thucydides); ὡς κώδωνα ἐξαψάμενος like one with an alarm-bell in his hand, (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

κωλυμα.definition: 1. a hindrance, impediment , (Euripides) 2. a defence against a thing, precaution , (Thucydides) (ML)

κωμαρχης.definition: the head man of a village , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

κωπη.definition: 1. any handle: 2. the handle of an oar , and generally an oar , (Odyssey by Homer), attic; νερτέρᾳ προσήμενος κώπῃ, = θαλαμίτης, metaphorically of a man of low rank, (Aeschulus Tragicus); παραπέμπειν ἐφ᾽ ἕνδεκα κώπαις, a proverb of dubious origin, meaning "to escort with all the honours, " (Aristophanes Comicus):—; poetry to express ships, σὺν κώπᾳ χιλιοναύτᾳ, of Agamemnon's fleet, (Euripides) 3. the handle of a sword, the haft, hilt , Lat. capulus , (Homer) 4. the handle of a key , (Odyssey by Homer) 5. the haft of a torch , (Euripides) (ML)

λαβη.definition: 1. the part intended for grasping, a handle, haft , (Demosthenes Orator); λαβαὶ ἀμφίστομοι of a cup, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. as a pugilistic term, a grip or hold , ὥσπερ ἀθλητὴς λαβὴν ζητεῖν (Plutarch):—; metaphorically a handle, occasion, opportunity , λαβὴν διδόναι, Lat. ausam praebere , (Aristophanes Comicus); so, λ. παραδιδόναι, παρέχειν (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

λαβρος.definition: 1. (Homer) of wind, rain, etc., furious, boisterous , (Herdotus Historicus); λ. πῦρ, κύματα, πόντος, etc., (Euripides) 2. after (Homer), of men, boisterous, turbulent, violent , (Theognis Elegiacus), etc. 3. greedy , (Pindar) 4. adverb λάβρως, violently, furiously , (Theognis Elegiacus) 5. greedily , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

λαθριος.definition: neuter plural as adverb , treacherously , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

λακκος.definition: 1. a pond for water-fowl, Lat. vivarium , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. a pit, reservoir , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

λαλημα.definition: 1. talk, prattle , (Moschus Bucolicus) 2. a prater , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

λαμπαδιον.definition: 1. a small torch , (Plato Philosophus) 2. a bandage for wounds, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

λαμπτηρ.definition: 1. a stand or grate for pine and other wood used for lighting rooms , (Odyssey by Homer); ὧ χαῖρε, λ. νυκτός thou that lightest up the night, of the beacon-fire, (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἕσπεροι λαμπτῆρες the evening watch-fires , (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. generally, = λαμπάς 1 (Euripides) (ML)

λαξευω.definition: to hew in stone , (Septuagint Greek Bible) (ML)

λαπτω.definition: 1. to lap with the tongue , of wolves, (Iliad by Homer) 2. to drink greedily, suck in , (Lucian) (ML)

λαρος.definition: 1. a ravenous sea-bird, perhaps a cormorant , described as dashing down into the sea and then floating on the waves, (Odyssey by Homer): metaphorically of demagogues, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. a singing bird, [ variant dates Anthology Palantina (ML)

λαφυρα.definition: spoils taken in war, Lat. spolia , [ variant dates Tragica Adespota , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

λεαινω.definition: 1. to smooth or polish , (Homer); ἵπποισι κέλευθον λειανέω I will smooth the way, (Iliad by Homer) 2. to rub smooth, pound in a mortar , Lat. levigare , (Herdotus Historicus); to grind with the teeth, (Xenophon Historicus):—; generally, to crush, extirpate , (Herdotus Historicus) 3. to smooth away wrinkles, (Plato Philosophus):—; metaphorically to smooth or soften down harsh words, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

λεβης.definition: 1. a kettle or caldron of copper, (Homer), etc. 2. a basin in which the purifying water χέρνιψ); was handed to the guests before meals, (Odyssey by Homer); also a pan for washing the feet, (Odyssey by Homer): a bath , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. a cymbal , (Herdotus Historicus) 4. a cinerary urn , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;generally, a casket , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

λειχην.definition: a tree-moss, lichen , then, a lichenlike eruption, canker, scurvy, blight , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

λειχω.definition: 1. to lick up , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. irregular participle perfect , γλώσσηισι λελειχμότες playing with their tongues, (Hesiod) (ML)

λεξις.definition: 1. a speaking, saying, speech , (Plato Philosophus) 2. a way of speaking, diction, style , (Plato Philosophus), etc. 3. κατὰ λέξιν as the phrase goes , [ variant dates Anthology Palantina (ML)

λεπτυνω.definition: to make small or fine: to thresh out, winnow , [ variant dates Anthology Palantina :—;Pass. to be reduced, grow lean , (Aristotle Philosopher); τοὺς ὤμους λεπτύνεσθαι (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

λεσχη.definition: 1. a place where people assembled to talk and hear news, a lounge, club-room , (Odyssey by Homer), etc.: —;also a council-hall, council , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. talk or gossip , such as went on in the λέσχαι, (Euripides):—; in good sense, conversation, discussion , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

λευκανθιζω.definition: to have white blossoms : generally, to be white or made white , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

λευκη.definition: 1. white leprosy , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 2. the white poplar , Lat. populus alba , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

λημμα.definition: anything received, income , (Aeschulus Tragicus); λ. καὶ ἀνάλωμα receipt and expense, (Plato Philosophus): generally, gain, profit , Lat. lucrum , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.; παντὸς ἥττων λήμματος unable to resist any temptation of gain , (Demosthenes Orator); often in plural , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

ληστηριον.definition: 1. a band of robbers , (Xenophon Historicus):—; a retreat or nest of robbers , (Strabo Geographus) 2. robbery , in plural , (Lucian) from λῃστής (ML)

λιθουργεω.definition: to turn into stone, petrify , [ variant dates Anthology Palantina from λῖθουργός (ML)

λιμα.definition: λιμά , T7, for λαμά - (Heb. מָה, seel. λεμά = Aram. לְמָא) why : (WH, mg., λεμά TTr., WH, txt., λεμά L), (λεμά LT, λαμμᾶ, Rec.).† (AS)

λιμοκτονεω.definition: to kill by hunger, starve , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

λιμωσσω.definition: to be famished, hungry , [ Refs 1st c.BC , variant dates Anthology Palantina (ML)

λινεος.definition: of flax, flaxen, linen , Lat. lineus , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. (ML)

λιπαινω.definition: 1. to oil, anoint : Mid. to anoint oneself , [ variant dates Anthology Palantina 2. of rivers, to make fat, enrich , (Euripides) (ML)

λισσομαι.definition: 1. to beg, pray, entreat, beseech , either absolute or with accusative pers., (Homer); that by which one prays, in genitive , λ. τινα γούνων (Iliad by Homer); λ. Ζηνός (Odyssey by Homer):—;an infinitive is often added, οὐδέ ς᾽ ἔγωγε λίσσομαι μένειν I do not pray thee to remain, (Iliad by Homer) 2. with accusative rei, to beg or pray for , οἷ αὐτῶι θάνατον λιτέσθαι (Iliad by Homer): with double accusative of persons or things , ταῦτα μὲν οὐχ ὑμέας ἔτι λίσσομαι this I beg of you no more, (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

λιτανευω.definition: to pray, entreat , especially for protection, either absolute or with accusative pers., (Homer); that by which one prays in genitive , γούνων λιτανεύειν (Odyssey by Homer); also, γούνων ἁψάμενοι λιτανεύσομεν (epic for -ωμεν); (Iliad by Homer); with infinitive , (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

λιτος.definition: 1. smooth, plain : of style, simple, unadorned , (Aristotle Philosopher): of persons, simple, frugal , (Polybius Historicus): adverb λιτῶς, [ variant dates Anthology Palantina 2. paltry, petty , [ variant dates Anthology Palantina (ML)

λοβος.definition: 1. the lobe of the ear , (Iliad by Homer) 2. the lobe of the liver , (Aeschulus Tragicus): generally, the liver , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

λοφια.definition: 1. the mane on the neck and back of certain animals, the mane of horses, the bristly back of boars and hyaenas, (Odyssey by Homer) 2. the back-fin of fishes, [ variant dates Anthology Palantina (ML)

λοχευω.definition: 1. to bring forth, bear , (Homeric Hymns):—;Pass. to be delivered, bear children , (Euripides); λοχευθεῖσα πυρί, of Semele, (Euripides) 3. Mid., just like Act., of the mother, (Euripides); of the birthplace, [ variant dates Anthology Palantina 4. Pass., of the child, to be brought forth, born , (Sophocles Tragicus); Προμα_θεῖ λοχευθεῖσα brought to birth by Prometheus, (Euripides): —; metaphorically , generally, to lie embedded , ἐν τεύτλοισι (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

λυπηρος.definition: 1. of things, painful, distressing , Lat. molestus , (Herdotus Historicus), attic 2. of persons, 3. in good sense, causing sorrow by one's departure, (Euripides) 4. in bad sense, causing pain, troublesome, vexatious, offensive , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc. 5. adverb λυπηρῶς, painfully, so as to cause pain , (Sophocles Tragicus); λυπηρῶς ἔχει it is painful , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

λωμα.definition: the border of a robe :—;Diminutive λωμάτιον, τό, [ variant dates Anthology Palantina (ML)

μα.definition: shortened doric form for μάτηρ, μᾶ γᾶ for μῆτερ γῆ, (Aeschulus Tragicus); μᾶ, πόθεν ἅνθρωπος; (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

μαγειρειον.definition: 1. a cook-shop , Lat. popina , (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. the place where the public cooks lived, the cooks' quarter , (Theophrastus Philosophus) (ML)

μαγειρευω.definition: 1. to be a cook, to cook meat , (Theophrastus Philosophus) 2. to be a butcher , (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor) (ML)

μαγειρος.definition: 1. a cook , (Herdotus Historicus), attic 2. a butcher , (Euripides) (From ! μαγ, Root of μάσσω ( q. see.), because baking bread was the business of the ancient cook.) (ML)

μαθημα.definition: 1. that which is learnt, a lesson , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 2. learning, knowledge, science , oft. in plural , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.: especially the mathematical sciences , (Plato Philosophus), etc. (ML)

μαια.definition: 1. good mother, dame , (Odyssey by Homer) 2. a fostermother, nurse , (Euripides):—;also a true mother , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. a midwife , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

μαιοομαι.definition: Dep. to deliver a woman, [ Refs 2nd c.AD , variant dates Anthology Palantina = μαιεύομαι (ML)

μακαριστος.definition: deemed or to be deemed happy, enviable , (Herdotus Historicus), attic (ML)

μακροβιος.definition: long-lived , (Aristotle Philosopher); μακροβιώτατος (Herdotus Historicus): —; οἱ M., an Ethiopian people, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

μακροθυμος.definition: longsuffering, patient , [ variant dates Anthology Palantina : adverb -μως, (New Testament) (ML)

μαλα.definition: 1. very, very much, exceedingly , (Homer), etc. 2. strengthening the word with which it stands, μάλα πολλά very many, (Homer); μάλα πάντες, μ. πᾶσαι, μ. πάντα, all together, every one , (Homer); μάλ᾽ ἀσκηθής all unhurt, (Odyssey by Homer); ἀβληχρὸς μάλα τοῖος so very weak, (Odyssey by Homer):—;so in attic, μάλα δὴ πρεσβύτης very old, (Xenophon Historicus); μ. γέ τινες ὀλίγοι (Plato Philosophus):—;so with Advs., πάγχυ μάλα and μάλα πάγχυ quite utterly, (Iliad by Homer); εὖ μάλα right well, (Odyssey by Homer); μάλ᾽ αἰεί for ever and aye, (Iliad by Homer); ἄχρι μάλα κνέφαος until quite dark, (Odyssey by Homer); μάλα διαμπερές right through, (Iliad by Homer):—;so in attic, to express repeated action, μάλ᾽ αὖθις, μάλ᾽ αὖ (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.:—; with Verbs, μή με μάλ᾽ αἴνεε praise me not greatly , (Iliad by Homer); ἡ δὲ μάλ᾽ ἡνιόχευεν she drove carefully , (Odyssey by Homer), etc. 3. strengthening an assertion, εἰ μάλα μιν χόλος ἵκοι if wrath come on him ever so much , (Homer); so μάλα περ with a participle , μάλα περ μεμαώς though desiring never so much , (Iliad by Homer) 4. in attic in answers, yes, certainly, exactly so , μάλα γε (Plato Philosophus), etc.; μ. τοι (Xenophon Historicus), etc.; καὶ μ. δή (Xenophon Historicus) 5. comparative μᾶλλον, more , (Homer); μᾶλλον τοῦ δέοντος more than is right, (Plato Philosophus), etc.; παντὸς μᾶλλον more than anything, i. e. most certainly, (Plato Philosophus) 6. denoting increase, more and more, still more , (Odyssey by Homer); μᾶλλον μᾶλλον, Lat. magis magisque , (Euripides) 7. sometimes joined to a second comparative , ῥηίτεροι μᾶλλον (Iliad by Homer); μᾶλλον ἆσσον (Sophocles Tragicus), etc. 8. μᾶλλον δέ, much more , but rather , πολλοί, μᾶλλον δὲ πάντες (Demosthenes Orator) 9. in μᾶλλον ἢ οὐ, οὐ seems redundant, ἥκει ὁ Πέρσης οὐδὲν μᾶλλον ἐπp ἡμέας ἢ οὐ ἐπp ὑμέας the Persians have come not more against us, than against you, (Herdotus Historicus); in this case μᾶλλον ἢ οὐ is preceded by another negative 10. τὸ μ. καὶ ἧττον, a form of argument, which we call a fortiori , (Aristotle Philosopher) 11. Sup. μάλιστα, most, most of all , (Homer), etc.; μάλιστα μέν . ., ἔπειτα δέ . ., first and above all . ., next . ., (Sophocles Tragicus):—; τί μάλιστ; what is the precise thing that you want? (Plato Philosophus); ὡς or ὅτι μ., Lat. quam maxime , (Plato Philosophus); ὅσον μ. (Aeschulus Tragicus); ὡς μ. certainly , in answers, (Plato Philosophus); ὡς δύναμαι μ. (Plato Philosophus); μακρῷ μ. (Herdotus Historicus) 12. ἐς τὰ μάλιστα for the most part, mostly , (Herdotus Historicus); so, τὰ μάλιστα (Thucydides), etc.; also, ἀνὴρ δόκιμος ὁμοῖα τῷ μ. as famous as he that is most [famous, Refs 5th c.BC ] 13. ἐν τοῖς μ. especially, as much as any , (Thucydides) 14. μάλιστα may be added to a Sup., ἔχθιστος μάλιστα, μάλιστα φίλτατος (Iliad by Homer); μ. φίλτατος (Euripides) 15. with numbers, μάλιστα means about , (Thucydides), etc.; so, ἐς μέσον μάλιστα about the middle, (Herdotus Historicus); ἥμισυ μ. (Thucydides), etc. 16. καὶ μάλιστα is used in answers, most certainly , Lat. vel maxime , (Aristophanes Comicus); so, μ γε (Sophocles Tragicus); μ. πάντων (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

μαλακιζομαι.definition: 1. to be softened or made effeminate, shew weakness or cowardice , (Thucydides) 2. to be softened or appeased , (Thucydides) (ML)

μανδρα.definition: 1. an inclosed space : 2. for cattle, a fold, byre, stable , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus), etc. 3. the setting of a ring , [ variant dates Anthology Palantina (ML)

μανιακης.definition: an armlet , worn of gold used by Persians and Gauls, (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

μαντεια.definition: 1. prophesying, prophetic power , (Homeric Hymns): mode of divination , (Herdotus Historicus); αἴνιγμα μαντείας ἔδει the riddle stood in need of divination , (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. = μαντεῖον II, (Tyrtaeus Elegiacus) (ML)

μαντειον.definition: 1. an oracle , i. e., 2. an oracular response , (Odyssey by Homer), attic 3. the seat of an oracle , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. (ML)

μαντις.definition: 1. one who divines, a seer, prophet , (Homer), etc.:—;as feminine a prophetess , [ variant dates Tragica Adespota , (Thucydides) 2. metaphorically a diviner, foreboder , (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. a kind of grasshopper , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

ματαιως.definition: acting in folly; for no cause

μαχητης.definition: a fighter, warrior , (Homer): doric adjective , μαχα_τάς, warlike , (Pindar) (ML)

μαχιμος.definition: fit for battle, warlike , (Herdotus Historicus), attic; οἱ μ. the fighting men, soldiery , and in Egypt the warrior-caste , (Herdotus Historicus); τὸ μ. the effective force , (Thucydides) (ML)

μεγαλοπρεπεια.definition: the character of a μεγαλοπρεπής, magnificence , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

μεγαλοφρων.definition: 1. high-minded, noble, generous , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. in bad sense, arrogant : adverb -όνως, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

μεθοδευω.definition: to treat by method: to use cunning devices, employ craft , (Septuagint Greek Bible) (ML)

μελαθρον.definition: 1. the ceiling of a room , or (rather) the main beam which bears the ceiling , (Odyssey by Homer); in (Odyssey by Homer) 19. 544, the end of this beam outside the house. 2. generally, a roof , (Homer) 3. a house, hall , (Pindar); mostly in plural , like Lat. tecta , [ variant dates Tragica Adespota derivation uncertain (ML)

μελετη.definition: 1. care, attention , (Hesiod); μ. πλεόνων care for many things, (Hesiod); ἔργων μ. attention to action, (Thucydides):—;but with genitive subjecti, care paid by one, θεῶν του μελέτῃ (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. practice, exercise , Lat. meditatio , (Pindar); ἡ δι᾽ ὀλίγου μ. their short practice , (Thucydides); πόνων μελέται painful exercises, of the Spartan discipline, (Thucydides) 3. in a military sense, exercise, practice, drill , (Thucydides) 4. of an orator, rehearsal , (Demosthenes Orator) 5. a pursuit , (Pindar) 6. care, anxiety , μελέτῃ κατατρύχεσθαι (Euripides) (ML)

μελιζω.definition: 1. to modulate, sing, warble , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus): mostly in Mid., (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

μελισσα.definition: 1. a bee , Lat. apis , (Homer), etc. 2. one of the priestesses of Delphi, (Pindar) 3. = μέλι, honey , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

μεμψις.definition: 1. blame, censure, reproof , μ. ἐπιφέρειν τινί (Aristophanes Comicus); ἔχειν μ. to incur blame , (Euripides) 2. active cause for complaint , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

μεσημβρινος.definition: 1. belonging to noon, about noon, noontide , εὖτε πόντος ἐν μεσημβριναῖς κοίταις εὕδοι πεσών (Aeschulus Tragicus); μεσημβρινοῖσι θάλπεσι in the noon-day heats, (Aeschulus Tragicus); ὁ μ. ᾠδός, of the cicada, [ variant dates Anthology Palantina :—; τὸ μεσαμβρινόν noon , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 2. southern , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

μεταβολη.definition: 1. a change, changing , (Pindar) 2. exchange, barter, traffic , (Thucydides) 3. (from Mid.) a transition, change , and in plural changes, vicissitudes , (Herdotus Historicus):—;with genitive change from a thing, μ. κακῶν (Euripides); rarely change to . . , μ. ἀπραγμοσύνης (Thucydides); but this is generally expressed by a preposition , ἅμα τῇ μ. ἐς Ἕλληνας their going over to the Greeks, (Herdotus Historicus); ἡ ἐναντία μ. change to the contrary, (Thucydides) 4. μ. τῆς ἡμέρης an eclipse , (Herdotus Historicus) 5. μ. πολιτείας change of government, a revolution , (Thucydides) 6. as military term, a wheeling about , (Polybius Historicus); metaphorically of a speaker, (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

μεταλλευω.definition: 1. to get by mining :—;Pass. to be got by mining , of metals, (Plato Philosophus), etc. 2. generally, to explore , [ variant dates Anthology Palantina (ML)

μεταμελεια.definition: change of purpose, regret, repentance , (Thucydides); μ. ἔχει με = μεταμέλει μοι, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

μετανιστημι.definition: 1. to remove one from his country , (Polybius Historicus) 2. Pass. with aorist2 et perfect active to move off and go elsewhere, to migrate , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

μεταπιπτω.definition: 1. to fall differently, undergo a change , μ. τὸ εἶδος (Herdotus Historicus), or εἰς ἄλλο εἶδος (Plato Philosophus): also, to change one's opinion suddenly , (Euripides); εἰ τρεῖς μόναι μετέπεσον τῶν ψήφων (Plato Philosophus) 2. to change , especially for the worse, μεταπίπτοντος δαίμονος if fortune changes , (Euripides); rarely for the better, (Euripides):—;of political changes, to undergo change or revolution , (Thucydides) (ML)

μετασκευαζω.definition: 1. to put into another dress σκευή); to change the fashion of, transform , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. Mid. to pack up so as to shift one's quarters , (Lucian) (ML)

μεταστροφη.definition: a turning from one thing to another , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

μεταφρενον.definition: properly, the part behind the midriff μετὰ τὰς φρένας); the back , (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

μετερχομαι.definition: 1. to come or go among others, with dative plural or absolute , (Homer); μετελθών having gone between the ranks , (Iliad by Homer) 2. to go to another place , (Iliad by Homer): simply to come next, follow , (Pindar) 3. with accusative to go after, to go to seek, go in quest of (Iliad by Homer), attic: generally, to seek for, aim at , (Euripides) 4. in hostile sense, to pursue , (Iliad by Homer), attic: with accusative rei, to seek to avenge , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;then with double accusative of persons or things , μ. τι τινά to visit a crime upon a person, (Euripides) 5. of things, to go after, attend to, to pursue a business, (Homer), attic 6. to approach with prayers , Lat. adire, prosequi , τινα (Herdotus Historicus): to court or woo , (Pindar) (ML)

μετεωρος.definition: 1. raised from the ground, hanging , Lat. suspensus , (Herdotus Historicus);—;of high ground, (Thucydides) 2. like μετάρσιος, in mid-air, high in air , Lat. sublimis , (Herdotus Historicus); Ἀήρ, ὃς ἔχεις τὴν γῆν μ. poised on high , (Aristophanes Comicus); τὰ μ. χωρία the regions of air , (Aristophanes Comicus); τὰ μ. things in heaven above, astronomical phenomena , (Aristophanes Comicus) 3. on the high sea, out at sea , of ships, (Thucydides) 4. metaphorically of the mind, lifted up, buoyed up, on the tiptoe of expectation, in suspense , Lat. spe erectus , (Thucydides) 5. wavering, uncertain , (Demosthenes Orator): —; adverb , μετεώρως ἔχειν to be in uncertainty , (Plutarch) (ML)

μετοικεω.definition: 1. to change one's abode, remove to a place, with accusative loci, (Euripides):—;with dative loci, to settle in , (Pindar) 2. absolute to be a μέτοικος or settler, reside in a foreign city , (Euripides), etc. (ML)

μετοικια.definition: 1. change of abode, removal, migration , (Thucydides) 2. a settling as μέτοικος, settlement or residence in a foreign city , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc. (ML)

μετοικος.definition: 1. changing one's abode, emigrating and settling elsewhere , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. as Substantive μέτοικος, ἡ, an alien settled in a foreign city, a settler, emigrant, sojourner , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.; μ. γῆς one who has settled in a country, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. at Athens, a resident alien , who paid a tax μετοίκιον); but enjoyed no civic rights, (Thucydides), etc. (ML)

μετριαζω.definition: 1. to be moderate, keep measure , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc. 2. transitive to moderate, regulate, control , Lat. moderari , (Plato Philosophus), etc. (ML)

μηνις.definition: wrath, anger , of the gods, (Homer), attic (ML)

μηνισκος.definition: a crescent , Lat. lunula : a covering to protect the head of statues (like the nimbus or glory of Christian Saints), (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

μηνιω.definition: to be wroth with another, vent one's wrath on him, with dative pers., (Iliad by Homer); with genitive rei, ἱρῶν μηνίσας wrathful because of sacred rites, (Iliad by Homer); πατρὶ μηνίσας φόνου (Sophocles Tragicus); absolute to be wrathful , (Homer): so in Mid., (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

μηρια.definition: 1. slices cut from the thighs , (Homer) It was the custom to cut out the μηρία ἐκ μηρία τάμνον); wrap them in two folds of fat κνίσῃ ἐκάλυψαν, δίπτυχα ποιήσαντες); and burn them upon the altar. 2. = μηροί, the thighs , (Bion Bucolicus) (ML)

μηρυομαι.definition: 1. Dep. 2. to draw up, furl sails, (Odyssey by Homer): to draw up cables, etc., [ variant dates Anthology Palantina :—; κρόκα ἐν στήμονι μηρύσασθαι to weave the woof into the warp, (Hesiod) 3. Pass., κισσὸς μαρύεται περὶ χείλη ivy winds round the edge, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

μηχανη.definition: 1. = Lat. machina : 2. an instrument, machine for lifting weights and the like, (Herdotus Historicus); μ. Ποσειδῶνος, of the trident, (Aeschulus Tragicus); λαοπόροις μ., of Xerxes' bridge of boats, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. an engine of war, (Thucydides) 4. a theatrical machine , by which gods were made to appear in the air, (Plato Philosophus): hence proverbial of any sudden appearance, ὥσπερ ἀπὸ μηχανῆς (cf. Lat. deus ex machina), (Demosthenes Orator) 5. any contrivance , for doing a thing, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.: in plural μηχαναί, shifts, devices, arts, wiles , (Hesiod), attic; μηχαναῖς Διός by the arts of Zeus, (Aeschulus Tragicus); proverbial , μηχαναὶ Σισύφου (Aristophanes Comicus):—;Phrases, μηχανήν or μηχανὰς προσφέρειν (Euripides); εὑρίσκειν (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.:—;with genitive , μ. κακῶν a contrivance against ills, (Euripides); but, μ. σωτηρίας a way of providing safety, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 6. οὐδεμία μηχανή [ ἐστι] ὅπως οὐ, with future , (Herdotus Historicus); also, μὴ οὐ, with infinitive , (Herdotus Historicus) 7. in adverb, phrases, ἐκ μηχανῆς τινος in some way or other, (Herdotus Historicus); μηδεμιῆι μηχανῆι by no means whatsoever, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

μιλτος.definition: red chalk, ruddle , Lat. rubrica , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

μισος.definition: 1. hate, hatred : and so, 2. passive hate borne one, a being hated , [ variant dates Tragica Adespota , (Plato Philosophus) 3. active hate felt against another, a grudge , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.; μ. τινός τινι felt by one against another, (Euripides) 4. of persons, a hateful object , = μίσημα, [ variant dates Tragica Adespota (ML)

μιτρα.definition: 1. a belt or girdle , worn round the waist beneath the cuirass (whereas the ζωστήρ went over it), (Iliad by Homer) 2. = ζώνη, the maiden-zone , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus), etc. 3. a girdle worn by wrestlers , [ variant dates Anthology Palantina 4. a head-band worn by Greek women to tie up their hair, a snood , (Euripides) 5. the victor's chaplet at the games, (Pindar); Λυδία μίτρα a Lydian garland (i. e. an ode in Lydian measure), (Pindar) 6. a Persian head-dress, turban , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

μνησικακεω.definition: 1. to remember wrongs done one, remember past injuries , (Herdotus Historicus); οὐ μν. to bear no malice, pass an act of amnesty , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.: with dative pers. et genitive rei, μ. τινί τινος to bear one a grudge for a thing, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. with accusative rei, τὴν ἡλικίαν μν. to remind one of the ills of age, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

μονιμος.definition: 1. staying in one's place, stable, steadfast , (Sophocles Tragicus); of soldiers, Lat. statarius , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. of things, conditions and the like, abiding, lasting, stable , Lat. stabilis , (Euripides), etc. (ML)

μονομαχεω.definition: to fight in single combat , (Euripides); τινι with one, (Herdotus Historicus); of the Athenians at Marathon, μοῦνοι μουνομαχήσαντες τῷ Πέρσῃ having fought single-handed with the Persians, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

μοχθεω.definition: 1. to be weary with toil, to be sore distressed , (Iliad by Homer):—; to work hard, labour , (Euripides), etc.; with accusative cognate , μ. μόχθους, πόνους to undergo hardships, or to execute painful tasks, (Euripides); μ. μαθήματα to toil at learning, (Euripides) 2. with accusative objecti, τέκνα ἁμόχθησα the children whom I toiled for, (Euripides); μ. τινά θεραπεύμασιν = θεραπεύειν, (Euripides); compare μόχθος. (ML)

μοχλος.definition: 1. a bar used as a lever, a crowbar, handspike , Lat, vectis , used for moving ships, (Odyssey by Homer); for forcing doors and gates, (Euripides) 2. the stake which Ulysses ran into the Cyclops' eye, (Odyssey by Homer) 3. a wooden bar , placed across gates on the inside and secured by the βάλανος, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

μυγαλη.definition: the shrew-mouse, field-mouse , Lat. mus araneus , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

μυια.definition: a fly , Lat. musca , (Iliad by Homer):—; proverbial , μυίης θάρσος, of excessive boldness, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

μυκτηρ.definition: 1. the nose, snout , (Aristophanes Comicus): in plural the nostrils , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. from the use of the nose to express ridicule, a sneerer , [ variant dates Anthology Palantina (ML)

μυλη.definition: 1. Lat. mola , a mill, a handmill turned by women, (Odyssey by Homer) 2. the nether millstone , (Aristophanes Comicus); the upper being ὄνος, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

μυριοπλασιος.definition: 0, 000 times as many as , with genitive , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

μυρμηξ.definition: 1. Lat. formica , the ant, (Hesiod), etc. 2. a beast of prey in India, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

μυρσινη.definition: 1. = μύρτος, (Pindar) 2. a branch or wreath of myrtle , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

μυς.definition: 1. Lat. mus , a mouse, (Batrachomyomachia); μ. ἀρουραῖος the field-mouse , or the hamster , (Herdotus Historicus); μῦς πίσσας γεύεται, proverbial of one who is tempted to eat and finds himself caught, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 2. a muscle of the body, Lat. musculus , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

μυσαρος.definition: 1. foul, dirty : hence, loathsome, abominable , (Euripides); τὸ μ. an abomination , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. of persons, defiled, polluted , (Euripides) (ML)

μυσταξ.definition: doric and Lacon. word, the upper lip, the moustache , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus): compare μάσταξ. (ML)

ναμα.definition: anything flowing, running water, a river, stream , [ variant dates Tragica Adespota , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

ναπη.definition: a wooded vale, dell , or glen , (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

ναρκαω.definition: to grow stiff or numb , Lat. torpere , (Iliad by Homer) from νάρκη (ML)

ναυτικος.definition: 1. seafaring, naval , ὁ ν. στρατός opposite to ὁ πεζός, (Herdotus Historicus); ν. λεώς (Aeschulus Tragicus); στόλος (Sophocles Tragicus); ν. ἐρείπια wrecks of ships , (Aeschulus Tragicus); ν. ἀναρχία among the seamen , (Euripides):—; τὸ ναυτικόν a navy, fleet , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 2. of persons, skilled in seamanship, nautical , ναυτικοὶ ἐγένοντο became a naval power , (Thucydides) 3. ἡ ναυτική (i.e. τέχνη); navigation, seamanship , (Herdotus Historicus); so, τὰ ναυτικά (Plato Philosophus);—;but, τὰ ναυτικά, also, naval affairs naval power , (Thucydides) 4. at Athens, ναυτικόν technically meant money borrowed or lent on bottomry , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. (ML)

νεανις.definition: 1. a young woman, girl, maiden , (Iliad by Homer) 2. as adjective youthful , (Euripides) 3. new , [ variant dates Anthology Palantina (ML)

νεβρος.definition: the young of the deer, a fawn , (Homer), etc.; πέδιλα νεβρῶν fawnskin brogues, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

νεικος.definition: 1. a quarrel, wrangle, strife , (Homer), etc. 2. strife of words, railing, abuse, a taunt, reproach , (Iliad by Homer) 3. a strife at law, dispute before a judge , (Odyssey by Homer) 4. battle, fight , (Homer); ν. φυλόπιδος (Odyssey by Homer); of dissensions between whole nations , νεῖκος πρὸς Καρχηδονίους (Herdotus Historicus) 5. cause of strife, matter of quarrel , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

νεμω.definition: 1. to deal out, distribute, dispense , of meat and drink, (Homer), etc.; of the gods, νέμει ὄλβον Ὀλύμπιος ἀνθρώποισιν (Odyssey by Homer); μοῖραν ν. τινί to pay one due respect, (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.:—;Pass., ἐπὶ τοὺς Ἕλληνας νέμεται is freely bestowed upon them, (Herdotus Historicus); κρέα νενεμημένα portions of meat, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. Mid. to distribute among themselves , and so, to have as one's portion, possess, enjoy , (Homer), etc. 3. to dwell in, inhabit , (Homer): absolute to dwell , (Herdotus Historicus) 4. to spend, pass , αἰῶνα, ἡμέραν (Pindar) 5. Act. much like Mid. to hold, possess , γῆν, χώραν, πόλιν (Herdotus Historicus), attic:—;Pass., of places, to be inhabited , (Herdotus Historicus); of a country, to maintain itself, be constituted , (Thucydides) 6. to hold sway, manage , (Herdotus Historicus):—; ν. οἴακα to manage the helm, (Aeschulus Tragicus); ν. ἰσχὺν ἐπὶ σκήπτροισι to support one's strength on staves, (Aeschulus Tragicus); ν. γλῶσσαν to use the tongue, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 7. like νομίζω, to hold, consider as so and so, σὲ νέμω θεόν (Sophocles Tragicus); προστάτην ν. τινά to take as one's patron, (Aristotle Philosopher) 8. of herdsmen, to pasture or graze their flocks, drive to pasture, tend , Lat. pascere , (Odyssey by Homer), attic, etc.:—; metaphorically , ν. χόλον (Sophocles Tragicus) 9. Mid., of cattle, to feed , i. e. go to pasture, graze , Lat. pasci , (Homer), etc.: with accusative cognate to feed on , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; of men, to eat , (Sophocles Tragicus); of fire, to consume, devour , (Iliad by Homer), etc.; of cancerous sores, to spread , ἐνέμετο πρόσω (Herdotus Historicus) 10. with accusative loci, ὄρη νέμειν to graze the hills [with cattle, 5th/4th c.BC ]: Pass., [ τὸ ὄρος] νέμεται βουσί (Xenophon Historicus) 11. metaphorically , πυρὶ νέμειν πόλιν to give a city to the flames, (Herdotus Historicus): Pass., πυρὶ χθὼν νέμεται the land is devoured by fire, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

νεοω.definition: to renovate, renew , νέωσον (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;Mid., τάφους ἐνεώσατο had them renewed , [ variant dates Anthology Palantina (ML)

νευμα.definition: a nod or sign , (Thucydides); νεύματος ἕνεκα for a mere nod , i. e. without cause , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

νευρα.definition: a string or cord of sinew, a bowstring , (Homer), etc. (ML)

νευρον.definition: 1. a sinew, tendon; in plural , the tendons of the feet , (Iliad by Homer) 2. metaphorically in plural , τὰ νεῦρα τῆς τραγῳδίας, of lyric odes, their sinews, vigour , (Aristophanes Comicus); τὰ νεῦρα τῶν πραγμάτων (Aeschines Orator) 3. gut, cord made of sinew , for fastening the head of the arrow to the shaft, (Iliad by Homer): the cord of a sling , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

νιτρον.definition: in (Herdotus Historicus) and attic λίτρον, carbonate of soda , (Herdotus Historicus) Prob. a foreign word. (ML)

νοημων.definition: 1. thoughtful, intelligent , (Odyssey by Homer) 2. in one's right mind , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

νομας.definition: 1. roaming about for pasture : οἱ Νομάδες roaming, pastoral tribes, Nomads , (Herdotus Historicus), attic; and as proper noun , Numidians , (Polybius Historicus) 2. feminine adjective grazing, feeding, at pasture , (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. metaphorically , κρῆναι νομάδες wandering streams, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

νομιμος.definition: 1. conformable to custom, usage , or law, customary, prescriptive, established, lawful, rightful , (Euripides):—; νόμιμόν [ ἐστί] τινι ποιεῖν τι (Xenophon Historicus) 2. νόμιμα, ων, τά, usages, customs , (Herdotus Historicus), attic 3. funeral rites , Lat. justa , (Thucydides) 4. adverb -μως, (Plato Philosophus): comparative -ώτερον (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

νοσερος.definition: ν. κοίτη a bed of sickness , (Euripides):—; adverb , νοσερῶς ἔχειν τὸ σῶμα (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

νωτοφορος.definition: carrying on the back : as Substantive a beast of burthen , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

νουθετημα.definition: admonition, warning , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.; τἀμὰ νουθετήματα given to me, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

νυκτερινος.definition: by night, nightly , Lat. nocturnus , (Aristophanes Comicus); ν. γενέσθαι to happen by night , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

νυκτερις.definition: a bat , Lat. vespertilio , (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

ξανθιζω.definition: to make yellow or brown , by roasting or frying, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

ξενιος.definition: 1. belonging to a friend and guest, hospitable , Ζεὺς ξένιος as protector of the rights of hospitality , (Iliad by Homer):—; τράπεζα ξ. the guests' table, (Odyssey by Homer); ξένιός τινι bound to him by ties of hospitality , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. ξείνια, attic ξένια, ων, τά, friendly gifts, meat and drink , given to the guest by his host, (Homer); ξένια παρέσχε δαῖτα as a friendly gift , (Aeschulus Tragicus); βοῦν ξένια ἔπεμψεν (Xenophon Historicus); ἐπὶ ξένια καλεῖν to invite any one to eat with you , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; metaphorically , θάνατος ξένιά σοι γενήσεται (Euripides) 3. foreign , (Pindar), attic (ML)

ξιφος.definition: a sword , (Homer); distinguished from μάχαιρα, q. see. (ML)

ξυρον.definition: a rasor , (Homer), etc.:—;proverb, ἐπὶ ξυροῦ ἵσταται ἀκμῆς ὄλεθρος ἠὲ βιῶναι death or life is balanced on a rasor's edge, (Iliad by Homer); ἐπὶ ξυροῦ τῆς ἀκμῆς ἔχεται ἡμῖν τὰ πράγματα (Herdotus Historicus); βεβὼς ἐπὶ ξυρῷ τύχης (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

ξυω.definition: 1. to scrape, plane, smooth or polish , (Odyssey by Homer): metaphorically , ξῦσαι ἀπὸ γῆρας to scrape off, get rid of old age, (Homeric Hymns):—; Mid., παλτὸν ξύσασθαι to shape oneself a javelin-shaft, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. to make smooth, work delicately , (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

οβελισκος.definition: 1. a small spit , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. 2. a coin stamped with a spit , (Plutarch) 3. the leg of a compass , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

οβολος.definition: an obol , as a weight, = 1/6th part of a δραχμή, worth rather more than three halfpence, (Aristophanes Comicus); ἐν δυοῖν ὀβολοῖν θεωρεῖν, as we might say "to sit in the shilling gallery, " (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

οδοιπορος.definition: a wayfarer, traveller , (Aeschulus Tragicus);—;in (Iliad by Homer), a fellow-traveller , or guide. (ML)

οδοποιεω.definition: 1. to make or level a road , (Xenophon Historicus):—; Pass., of roads, to be made fit for use , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. metaphorically to reduce to a system , τι (Aristotle Philosopher) 3. with dative pers. to act as pioneer, serve as guide , (Xenophon Historicus):—;Pass. to make one's way, advance , Lat. progredi , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

οδυρομαι.definition: 1. to lament, bewail, mourn for : 2. with accusative pers., (Homer); with accusative rei, ὁ δ᾽ ὀδύρετο πατρίδα γαῖαν mourned for it, i. e. for the want of it, (Odyssey by Homer); so, νόστον ὀδυρομένη (Odyssey by Homer) 3. with genitive pers. to mourn for, for the sake of , (Homer) 4. with dative pers. to wail or lament to or before others, (Homer) 5. absolute to wail, mourn , (Homer) (ML)

οιακιζω.definition: to steer , and so to guide, manage , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

οικειοτης.definition: 1. kindred, relationship , (Herdotus Historicus), attic: intimacy, friendliness, kindness , (Thucydides):—;in plural friendly relations , (Demosthenes Orator) 2. of words, the proper sense , (Plutarch) (ML)

οικετις.definition: 1. feminine of οἰκέτης, (Euripides) 2. the mistress of the house , Lat. matrona , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

οικησις.definition: 1. the act of dwelling, habitation , (Herdotus Historicus), attic 2. management, administration , (Plato Philosophus) 3. a house, dwelling, residence , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; κατασκαφὴς οἴκ. of the grave, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

οικητωρ.definition: 1. an inhabitant , (Herdotus Historicus), attic; οἰκ. θεοῦ one who dwells in the temple of the god, (Euripides); Ἅιδου οἰκ., of one dead, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. a colonist , (Thucydides) (ML)

οικιζω.definition: 1. with accusative rei, to found as a colony or new settlement , πόλιν (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—; Pass., πόλις οἴκισται (Herdotus Historicus) 2. to people with new settlers, colonise , χώρην (Herdotus Historicus); νήσους (Thucydides):—;Mid. ὅπη γῆς πύργον οἰκιούμεθα in what part of the world we shall make ourselves a fenced home, (Euripides) 3. with accusative pers. to remove, transplant , (Euripides); metaphorically , τὸν μὲν ἀφ᾽ ὑψηλῶν βραχὺν ὤικισεν brought him from high to low estate, (Euripides):—;Pass. to settle in a place, (Euripides) (ML)

οικογενης.definition: born in the house, homebred , of slaves, Lat. verna , (Plato Philosophus); of quails, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

οικοπεδον.definition: 1. the site of a house , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. 2. the house itself, a building , (Thucydides) (ML)

οικτος.definition: pity, compassion , (Odyssey by Homer), Dht., attic:—;with genitive objecti, compassion for , οἶκτος τῆς πόλιος (Herdotus Historicus) the expression of pity, lamentation, piteous wailing , (Aeschulus Tragicus);—;and in plural , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

οικτρος.definition: 1. pitiable, in piteous plight , (Iliad by Homer), etc. 2. of things, pitiable, piteous, lamentable , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 3. in active sense, piteous , (Odyssey by Homer); οἰκτρᾶς γόον ὄρνιθος, of the nightingale, (Sophocles Tragicus);—; neuter plural as regularly adverb οἰκτρῶς, (Aeschulus Tragicus) —;Besides comparative and Sup. οἰκτρότερος, -τατος, (Homer) has an irreg. Sup. οἴκτιστος (q. see.). (ML)

οιμοι.definition: exclamation of pain, fright, pity, anger, grief, also of surprise, properly οἴ μοι ah me! woe's me! (Theognis Elegiacus);—;with genitive causae, οἴμοι τῶν κακῶν, οἴμοι γέλωτος ah me for my misfortunes, for the laughter, [ variant dates Tragica Adespota The last syllable in οἴμοι may be elided before ὡς. (ML)

οινοχοη.definition: a can for ladling wine from the mixing bowl κρατήρ); into the cups, (Hesiod) (ML)

οινοω.definition: 1. to intoxicate , οἰνῶσαι σῶμα ποτοῖς (Critias Philosophus) 2. Pass. οἰνόομαι to get drunk, be drunken , οἰνωθέντες (Odyssey by Homer); perfect participle , ᾠνωμένος, ionic οἰνωμένος, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

οιχομαι.definition: 1. Dep. to be gone, to have gone , Lat. abesse (not abire) , in perfect sense, and imperfect ὠιχόμην in pluperfect sense, directly opposite to ἥκω, to have come , while ἔρχομαι, to go or come , serves as the present to both, (Homer), etc.;—;often with participle , οἴχεται φεύγων is fled and gone , (Iliad by Homer); ὤιχετ᾽ ἀποπτάμενος he hath taken flight and gone , (Iliad by Homer); οἴχεται θανών (see. infr. II. 1); also with an adjective , οἴχεται φροῦδος he's clean gone, (Aristophanes Comicus):—;with accusative pers. to have escaped from , (Iliad by Homer) 2. Special usages, 3. euphamistic for θνήσκω, to be gone hence , οἴχεται εἰς Ἀί̈δαο (Iliad by Homer); in attic, οἴχεται θανών (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.:—; participle οἰχόμενος for θανών, departed, dead , [ variant dates Tragica Adespota ; but in (Homer) simply absent or away , Ὀδυσῆος πόθος οἰχομένοιο desire of the absent Ulysses, (Odyssey by Homer) 4. to be undone, ruined , (Sophocles Tragicus); especially in ὤιχωκα or οἴχωκα, Lat. perii , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc. 5. of things, to denote any quick, violent motion, to rush, sweep along , (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

οιωνιζομαι.definition: 1. Dep. 2. to take omens from the flight and cries of birds , Lat. augurium, capere , (Xenophon Historicus) 3. generally, to divine from omens, augur , with accusative et infinitive , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

οιωνισμα.definition: divination by the flight or cries of birds , Lat. augurium , (Euripides) (ML)

οιωνος.definition: 1. a large bird, bird of prey , such as a vulture or eagle , and so distinguished from a common bird ὄρνις); (Homer), etc. 2. a bird of omen or augury , (Homer), etc.:—;the flight to (not from) the right, i. e. towards the East, was fortunate, and vice versa. 3. an omen, presage , drawn from these birds, Lat. auspicium or augurium , according as taken from seeing their flight or hearing their cry , (Iliad by Homer), etc.; δέκομαι τὸν οἰωνόν I accept the omen , hail it as favourable, (Herdotus Historicus) commonly derivation from οἶος, —; most birds of prey being solitary, —; compare κοινωνός from κοινός (ML)

οκλαζω.definition: to crouch down on one's hams, to squat , (Xenophon Historicus): ἐς γόνυ ὀκλάσας δέχεται τῇ σαρίσσῃ τὴν ἐπέλασιν, of a soldier waiting an attack, (Lucian); of a weary traveller, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;with accusative , ὀκλ. τὰ ὀπίσθια, τοὺς προσθίους to bend their hind or fore legs, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

οκτακισχιλιοι.definition: eight thousand , (Herdotus Historicus); in singular , ἵππος ὀκτακισχιλίη "8000 horse, " (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

οκτωκαιδεκατος.definition: eighteenth : ὀκτωκαιδεκάτῃ (i.e. ἡμέρᾳ); on the eighteenth day , (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

ολεθριος.definition: ὀλέθριος , -ον (also -α, -ον, as in Wis, l.with), [in LXX : (חֵרֶם), * ;] destructive, deadly : δίκην, , L, txt (for ὄλωεθρος, which see).† (AS)

ολεκω.definition: epic imperfect ὄλεκον, ionic ὀλέκεσκον, like ὄλλυμι, to ruin, destroy, kill , (Homer) (ML)

ολιγοστος.definition: 1. one out of a few , opposite to πολλοστός, (Plutarch) 2. ὀλ. χρόνον for the smallest space of Time, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

ολιγοτης.definition: 1. of Number, fewness , (Plato Philosophus) 2. of Amount, smallness, scantiness :—;of Time, shortness , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

ολισθανω.definition: 1. to slip, slip and fall , (Iliad by Homer); ἐξ ἀντύγων ὤλισθε he slipped from the chariot, (Sophocles Tragicus):—; metaphorically to make a slip , (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. to slip or glide along , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

ολκη.definition: a drawing, dragging, tugging: a drawing on or towards a thing, attraction, force of attraction , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

ολλυμι.definition: 1. Act. = Lat. perdo , 2. to destroy, make an end of , (Homer) 3. to lose , θυμόν, ψυχήν, μένος, ἦτορ ὀλέσαι to lose life, (Homer); πόνον ὀλέσαντες having lost their labour, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 4. Mid., = Lat. pereo , 5. to perish, come to an end , (Homer); also with accusative cognate , κακὸν οἶτον, κακὸν μόρον ὀλέσθαι to die by an evil death, (Iliad by Homer):—; ὄλοιο, ὄλοισθε may'st thou, may ye, perish! an imprecation, [ variant dates Tragica Adespota ; so, ὀλοίμην, ὄλοιτο, ὄλοιντο, (Sophocles Tragicus) 6. to be ruined, undone , (Homer), attic 7. of things, to be lost , (Homer) 8. perfect ὄλωλα, in sense of Mid., to have perished, to be undone, ruined , (Iliad by Homer), etc.; τῶν ὀλωλότων of the dead , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

ολολυγμος.definition: a loud crying , mostly a joyous cry , in honour of the gods, (Aeschulus Tragicus);—;rarely of lamentation , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

ολυρα.definition: mostly in plural ὄλυραι, a kind of grain, spelt or rye , (Iliad by Homer); compare ζειά. (ML)

ομαλιζω.definition: 1. to make even or level , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. to level, equalise , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

ομηρος.definition: 1. a pledge for the maintenance of unity, a surety, a hostage , (Herdotus Historicus), attic 2. of things, a pledge, security , τὴν γῆν ὅμηρον ἔχειν (Thucydides) derivation uncertain (ML)

ομομητριος.definition: born of the same mother , Lat. frater uterinus , (Herdotus Historicus); ὁμοματρία ἀδελφή (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

ομονοεω.definition: 1. to be of one mind, agree together, live in harmony , (Thucydides); ὁμονοοῦσα ὀλιγαρχία a united oligarchy, (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. with dative to live in harmony with others, with dative , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

ομονοια.definition: oneness of mind or thought, unity, concord , (Thucydides), etc. from ὁμόνους (ML)

ομορεω.definition: ionic ὁμουρέω, future -ήσω to border upon, march with , [ οἱ Κελτοὶ, ὁμουρέουσι Κυνησίοισι (Herdotus Historicus) from ὅμορος (ML)

ομορος.definition: 1. having the same borders with, marching with, bordering on , τοῖσι Δωριεῦσι, τῇ Λιβύῃ (Herdotus Historicus); absolute bordering , (Thucydides); πόλεμος ὅμορος a border war, (Demosthenes Orator) 2. metaphorically bordering on, closely resembling , (Aristotle Philosopher) 3. also as Substantive , a neighbour , (Herdotus Historicus); κατὰ τὸ ὅμορον because of their neighbourhood , (Thucydides) (ML)

ομφαλος.definition: 1. the navel , Lat. umbilicus , (Iliad by Homer), etc. 2. anything central (like a navel) : 3. the knob or boss in the middle of the shield, Lat. umbo , (Iliad by Homer) 4. a button or knob on the horse's yoke to fasten the reins to, (Iliad by Homer) 5. in plural the knobs at each end of the stick round which books were rolled , Lat. umbilici , (Lucian) 6. the centre or middle point , as the island of Calypso is the ὀμφαλός of the sea, (Odyssey by Homer); and Delphi (or rather a round stone in the Delphic temple) was called ὀμφαλός as marking the middle point of Earth , (Pindar), etc. (ML)

ομφαξ.definition: an unripe grape , πάροιθε δέ τ᾽ ὄμφακές εἰσιν (Odyssey by Homer); ὅτ᾽ ὄμφακες αἰόλλονται (Hesiod); ὅταν δὲ τεύχῃ Ζεὺς ἀπp ὄμφακος οἶνον, i. e. autumn, when the unripe grapes become fit to make wine, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

ονησις.definition: use, profit, advantage, good luck , (Odyssey by Homer):—;with genitive rei, enjoyment of a thing, profit or delight from it, (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.; so, ὄν. εὑρεῖν ἀπό τινος (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

ονομαστος.definition: 1. named, to be named , and οὐκ ὀνομαστός not to be named or mentioned , i. e. abominable , Lat. infandus , (Odyssey by Homer) 2. of name or note, notable, famous , (Theognis Elegiacus), etc. (ML)

ονυξ.definition: 1. Lat. unguis , in (Homer) only in plural of the eagle's talons;—; of human beings, a nail , (Hesiod), attic:—;of horses and oxen, a hoof , (Xenophon Historicus)—;Special phrases, εἰς ἄκρους τοὺς ὄνυχας ἀφίκετο (i.e. ὁ οἶνος); warmed me to my fingers' ends , (Euripides); ὄνυχας ἐπ᾽ ἄκρους στάς on tiptoe , Lat. summis digitis , (Euripides); ἐξ ἁπαλῶν ὀνύχων from childhood, (Horace) de tenero ungui , [ variant dates Anthology Palantina ; ὀδοῦσι καὶ ὄνυξι, i. e. in every possible way, (Lucian) 2. a veined gem, onyx , (Lucian) (ML)

οξυθυμος.definition: quick to anger, choleric , (Euripides), etc.: —; sharp to punish , of the Areopagus, (Aeschulus Tragicus): τὸ ὀξύθυμον, by crasis τοὐξύθυμον, = ὀξυθυμία, (Euripides) (ML)

οξυνω.definition: 1. to sharpen : metaphorically to goad to anger, provoke , (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Pass., (Herdotus Historicus) 2. to sharpen, quicken , [ variant dates Anthology Palantina (ML)

οξυτης.definition: 1. sharpness, pointedness , (Plato Philosophus) 2. of sound, sharpness , opposite to βαρύτης, (Plato Philosophus) 3. of the mind, sharpness, cleverness , (Plato Philosophus) 4. of motion, quickness , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

οπισθιος.definition: hinder, belonging to the hinder part , Lat. posticus , τὰ ὀπ. σκέλεα the hind- legs, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

οπλη.definition: a hoof, the solid hoof of the horse and ass, (Iliad by Homer), attic:—;after (Homer), like χηλή, the cloven hoof of horned cattle, (Homeric Hymns), etc. (ML)

οπλιτης.definition: 1. heavy-armed, armed , δρόμος ὁπλ. a race of men in armour , opposite to the naked race, (Pindar); ὁπλ. στρατός an armed host, (Euripides); ὁπλ. κόσμος warrior- dress, armour, (Euripides) 2. as Substantive , a heavy-armed foot-soldier, man-at-arms , who carried a large shield ὅπλον); whence the name, as the light-armed foot-soldier πελταστής); had his from the light πέλτη, (Herdotus Historicus), attic; ὁπλῖται are opposite to ψιλοί, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

οπλομαχος.definition: 1. fighting in heavy arms , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. ὁπλ., one who teaches the use of arms, a drill-sergeant , (Theophrastus Philosophus) (ML)

οπλοφορος.definition: 1. bearing arms: a warrior, soldier , (Euripides) 2. = δορυφόρος, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

οπταω.definition: 1. to roast, broil , (Homer), etc.; with genitive partitive , ὀπτῆσαί τε κρεῶν to roast some meat, (Odyssey by Homer):—; ὀπτᾶν was used of cooking by means of fire or dry heat , opposite to ἕψω to boil in water , which never appears in (Homer); and a [ variant dates Comica Adespota poet remarks that Homer's heroes ate only roast meat:—;Pass., aor1 infinitive ὀπτηθῆναι (Odyssey by Homer) 2. to bake bread, (Herdotus Historicus):—;also of bricks or pottery, to bake, burn , (Herdotus Historicus) 3. to bake, harden , of the sun, (Bion Bucolicus) 4. metaphorically in Pass. to be burned by love, [ Refs 3rd c.BC , variant dates Anthology Palantina (ML)

οργανον.definition: 1. an organ, instrument, tool, for making or doing a thing, (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.:—;of a person, ἁπάντων ἀεὶ κακῶν ὄργ. (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. an organ of sense , (Plato Philosophus) 3. a musical instrument , (Plato Philosophus) 4. a surgical instrument , (Xenophon Historicus) 5. a work, product , λαί̈νεα Ἀμφίονος ὄργανα the stony works of Amphion, i. e. walls of Thebes, (Euripides) (ML)

ορθοω.definition: 1. to set straight : 2. in height, to set upright, set up one fallen or lying down, raise up , (Iliad by Homer); ὀρθοῦν κάρα, πρόσωπον (Euripides):—;of buildings, to raise up, rebuild , or, generally, to erect, build up , (Euripides):—;Pass. to be set upright , (Iliad by Homer), etc.: simply to rise from one's seat, stand up , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. in line, to make straight , (Aristotle Philosopher):—; Pass., ἢν τόδ᾽ ὀρθωθῆι βέλος if this dart go straight , (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. metaphorically (from signf. I) to raise up, restore to health, safety, happiness , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;also to exalt, honour , (Pindar) 5. (from signf. II) to guide aright , (Aeschulus Tragicus); ὀρθ. ἀγῶνας to bring to a happy end , (Aeschulus Tragicus); ὀ. βίον (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Pass. to succeed, prosper , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; τὸ ὀρθούμενον success , (Thucydides):—;of words and opinions, to be right, true , (Herdotus Historicus); ἐν ἀγγέλωι κρυπτὸς ὀρθοῦται λόγος a secret message is rightly sent by messenger, not by letter, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 6. in Pass. also, to be upright, deal justly , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

ορισμος.definition: 1. a marking out by boundaries, limitation , (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. the definition of a word , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

ορμος.definition: 1. a cord, chain , especially a necklace, collar , (Homer), attic 2. generally, anything strung like a necklace, a wreath, chaplet , (Pindar); στεφάνων ὅρμος a string of crowns, i. e. of praises, (Pindar) 3. a dance performed in a ring , (Lucian) 4. a roadstead, anchorage, moorings , (Iliad by Homer), attic 5. metaphorically a haven, place of shelter or refuge , [ Refs 5th c.BC , variant dates Anthology Palantina 6. = ἕρμα 1, [ variant dates Anthology Palantina (ML)

οροδαμνος.definition: a branch , [ variant dates Anthology Palantina derivation uncertain (ML)

ορτυγομητρα.definition: a bird which migrates with the quails , perhaps the land-rail , ludicrously applied to Latona, the Ortygian mother (compare Ὀρτυγία)), (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

ορφανια.definition: 1. orphanhood , (Plato Philosophus) 2. bereavement, want of , στεφάνων (Pindar) (ML)

οσιοω.definition: to make holy, purify, set free from guilt by offerings , Lat. expiate , (Euripides):—;Mid., στόμα ὁσιοῦσθαι to keep one's tongue pure , not to speak profanely, (Euripides):—;Pass. to be purified , (Plutarch) (ML)

οστρακον.definition: 1. an earthen vessel , Lat. testa , (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. a tile or potsherd , especially the tablet used in voting (see. ὀστρακίζω); (Plato Philosophus) 3. a sort of earthenware castanet , (Aristophanes Comicus) 4. the hard shell of testaceous animals , as snails, muscles, tortoises, (Homeric Hymns) (ML)

οσφραινομαι.definition: to catch scent of, smell, scent, track , with genitive , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; absolute , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

ουδαμου.definition: 1. nowhere , answering to πο; where? (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; with genitive , οὐδαμοῦ γῆς (Herdotus Historicus); οὐδαμοῦ ἦν φρενῶν (Euripides) 2. οὐδαμοῦ λέγειν τινά to esteem as naught , Lat. nullo in loco habere , (Sophocles Tragicus); so, θεοὺς νομίζων οὐδ. (Aeschulus Tragicus); οὐδ. (or μηδαμοῦ); εἶναι, φαίνεσθαι, like Cicero's ne apparere quidem, not to be taken into account , (Plato Philosophus) 3. of Manner, ἄλλοθι οὐδαμοῦ in no other way , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

ουριος.definition: 1. with a fair wind , Lat. vento secundo , οὔρ. πλοῦς, δρόμος a prosperous voyage, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. metaphorically prosperous, successful , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—; neuter plural οὔρια as adverb , (Euripides) 3. prospering, favouring, fair , of winds, (Euripides); comically of the bellows, οὐρίᾳ ῥιπίδι (Aristophanes Comicus) 4. οὐρία (i.e. πνοή); = οὖρος, a fair wind , οὐρίᾳ ἐφιέναι (i.e. ἑαυτόν); to run before the wind, (Plato Philosophus); so, ἐξ οὐρίων δραμοῦσα (i.e. δρόμων); after having run a fair course , (Sophocles Tragicus); ἀφήσω ἐμαυτὸν οὔριον (Aristophanes Comicus) 5. Ζεὺς οὔριος, as sending fair winds , i. e. conducting things to a happy issue , [ 6th/5th c.BC , variant dates Anthology Palantina (ML)

οχθη.definition: older form of ὄχθος, a rising ground, a bank, dyke by the side of a river, (Iliad by Homer): mostly in plural the raised banks of a river , (Homer); ὄχθαι καπέτοιο the banks of the trench, (Iliad by Homer); also the dunes or denes along the sea (compare θίς); (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

οχυρος.definition: 1. like ἐχυρός, firm, lasting, stout , (Hesiod) 2. of places, strong, secure , (Euripides): especially of a stronghold or position, strong, tenable , (Xenophon Historicus) 3. adverb -ρῶς, (Euripides) (ML)

οχυροω.definition: to make fast and sure, fortify , (Polybius Historicus): —;the Mid. just like Act., (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

οψιζω.definition: to do, go or come late , (Xenophon Historicus):—; Pass., ὀψισθέντες belated, benighted , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

οψον.definition: 1. properly, cooked meat , or, generally, meat , opposite to bread and other provisions, (Homer) 2. anything eaten with bread or food , to give it flavour and relish, κρόμυον, ποτῷ ὄψον onions, a zest or relish to wine, (Iliad by Homer); ἐσθίουσι ἐπὶ τῷ σίτῳ ὄψον (Xenophon Historicus) 3. seasoning, sauce , (Plato Philosophus); κολλύραν καὶ κόνδυλον ὄψον ἐπ᾽ αὐτῇ pudding and knuckle- sauce withal, (Aristophanes Comicus); λιμῷ ὅσαπερ ὄψῳ διαχρῆσθε, i. e. "hunger is the best sauce," (Xenophon Historicus) 4. generally, dainty fare , in plural dainties , (Plato Philosophus) 5. at Athens, mostly, fish , the chief dainty of the Athenians, (Aristophanes Comicus) 6. the fish-market , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

παγος.definition: Πάγος , see: Ἄρειος. Ἄρειος Πάυος (T, Ἄριος Π.), -ου, ὁ Hill of Pres or Mars, Areopagus; also, the Court of Areopagus, the highest tribunal of Athens : .† (AS)

παιγνιον.definition: 1. a plaything, toy , (Plato Philosophus) 2. in (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus), the Egyptians are called κακὰ παίγνια roguish playmates , 3. a game, a sportive poem , [ variant dates Anthology Palantina ; of the merry chirp of the cicada, [ variant dates Anthology Palantina (ML)

παλαθη.definition: a cake of preserved fruit , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

παλαιω.definition: to wrestle , (Iliad by Homer): π. τινί to wrestle with one, (Odyssey by Homer):—;Pass., παλαισθείς beaten , (Euripides) (ML)

παλλακις.definition: a concubine, mistress , Lat. pellex , opposite to a lawful wife κουριδίη ἄλοχος); (Homer) Prob. from same Root as παλλάς = νεᾶνις. (ML)

παλλω.definition: 1. to poise or sway a missile before it is thrown, (Euripides) 2. to sway other arms, not missiles, σάκος (Hesiod); πέλτας (Euripides):—;then, to toss a child, (Iliad by Homer); Νὺξ ὄχημm ἔπαλλεν she drave it furiously , (Euripides) 3. κλήρους ἐν κυνέηι πάλλον they shook the lots together in a helmet, till one leapt forth, (Homer): absolute to cast lots , (Iliad by Homer); ὅθ᾽ αὐτοὺς οἱ βραβεῖς κλήροις ἔπηλαν where the stewards ranged them by casting lots, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Mid. to draw lots , ἔλαχον ἅλα παλλομένων I obtained the sea when we cast lots , (Iliad by Homer); so in (Herdotus Historicus) 4. Pass. to swing or dash oneself , ἐν ἄντυγι πάλτο he dashed himself upon the shield-rim, (Iliad by Homer): to quiver, leap , especially in fear, πάλλεται ἦτορ (Iliad by Homer); also of the person, παλλομένη κραδίην (Iliad by Homer); of dying fish, to quiver, leap , (Herdotus Historicus) 5. intransitive , like the Pass., to leap, bound , (Euripides): to quiver , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

πανδημει.definition: with the whole people, in a mass or body , (Herdotus Historicus); π. βοηθεῖν, στρατεύειν, of a whole people going out to war, a levee en masse , (Thucydides) (ML)

πανηγυριζω.definition: to celebrate or attend a festival , πανηγύρις π. to keep holy-days , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

πανοικια.definition: with all the house, household and all , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

παντοδαπος.definition: 1. of every kind, of all sorts, manifold , (Homeric Hymns), etc.:—;in plural , πολλοὶ καὶ π. (Herdotus Historicus):—; adverb -πῶς, in all kinds of ways , Poeta quoted in (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. παντοδαπὸς γίγνεται, = παντοῖος γίγνεται, assumes every shape , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

παπυρος.definition: 1. the papyrus , an Egyptian rush with triangular stalks: paper was made by peeling off its outer coat βύβλος); and gluing the slips together. 2. anything made of it, linen, cord , etc., [ variant dates Anthology Palantina (ML)

παραβλεπω.definition: 1. to look aside, take a side look , (Aristophanes Comicus); π. θατέρῳ (i.e. ὀφθαλμῷ); to look suspiciously with one eye, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. to see wrong , (Lucian) (ML)

παραγγελμα.definition: 1. a message transmitted by beacons, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. an order, command , ἀπὸ παραγγέλματος by word of command , (Thucydides) 3. an instruction, precept , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

παραδειγμα.definition: 1. a pattern or model of the thing to be executed, Lat. exemplar , an architect's plan , (Herdotus Historicus); a sculptor's or painter's model , (Plato Philosophus) 2. a precedent, example , (Thucydides); ἐπὶ παραδείγματος by way of example , (Aeschines Orator) 3. an example , i. e. a lesson or warning , π. ἔχειν τινός to take a lesson from another, (Thucydides); τὸ σὸν π. ἔχων (Sophocles Tragicus); ζῶντά τινα τοῖς λοιποῖς π. ποιεῖν (Demosthenes Orator) 4. an argument, proof from example , (Thucydides) 5. the model or copy of an existing thing, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

παραδεικνυμι.gloss: to hold forth as an example
παραδεικνυμι.definition: 1. to exhibit side by side : generally, to exhibit, bring forward , in Mid., (Demosthenes Orator) 2. to represent as so and so, π. τινὰ οὐκ ὄντα (Polybius Historicus): also in bad sense, like παραδειγματίζω, (Plutarch) 3. to exhibit and hand over , τί τινι (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

παραδοξαζω.definition: to do an incredible thing; render notorious

παραδρομη.definition: a running beside or over, traversing , (Plutarch); ἐν παραδρομῇ cursorily , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

παραθερμαινω.definition: to heat to excess :—;Pass., aor1 participle παραθερμανθείς, of a man become quarrelsome in his cups, (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

παραθεσις.definition: juxta-position, neighbourhood , (Polybius Historicus); ἐκ παραθέσεως on comparison , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

παραιρεω.definition: 1. to take away from beside, withdraw, remove , (Euripides):—; with genitive partitive to take away part of a thing, (Euripides):—;Pass., παρῃρημένοι τὰ ὅπλα having their arms taken from them, (Thucydides) 2. π. ἀρὰν εἰς παῖδα to draw aside the curse on thy son's head, (Euripides) 3. Mid. to draw over to one's own side, seduce, detach , (Xenophon Historicus) 4. to take away , (Xenophon Historicus): Mid., παραιρεῖσθαι τὴν θρασύτητα to lessen, damp it, (Demosthenes Orator) 5. generally, to take away from, steal away from , τί τινος (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

παρακαθημαι.definition: Dep. to be seated beside or near another, with dative , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. (ML)

παρακελευομαι.definition: 1. Dep. 2. to order one to do a thing, advise, prescribe , τί τινι (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; π. ταῦτα to give this advice , (Plato Philosophus);—;also, π. τινι, with infinitive , (Plato Philosophus) 3. to exhort , τοιαῦτα παρακελευσάμενος having delivered this address , (Thucydides):—; absolute to encourage one another by shouting , (Herdotus Historicus) 4. παρακεκέλευστο in passive sense, orders had been given , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

παρακρουω.definition: 1. to strike aside: to disappoint, mislead , (Plato Philosophus):—;Pass. to be led astray, go wrong , (Plato Philosophus):—;so also in Mid., (Isocrates Orator) 2. in Mid. also, to strike away from oneself, parry , (Plutarch) (ML)

παραλλαξις.definition: 1. alternation, alternating motion , τῶν σκελῶν (Plutarch) 2. a change for the worse, alteration , (Plato Philosophus) from παραλλάσσω (ML)

παραλλασσω.definition: 1. to make things alternate, to transpose , (Plato Philosophus) 2. to change or alter a little , (Herdotus Historicus) 3. of Place, to pass by, go past, elude , (Xenophon Historicus):—; to get rid of , (Plutarch) 4. to go beyond, exceed in point of time, (Plutarch) 5. intransitive to pass by one another, to overlap , (Herdotus Historicus) 6. to differ, vary , (Herdotus Historicus):—; impersonal , οὐ σμικρὸν παραλλάττει it makes no small difference , (Plato Philosophus) 7. π. τοῦ σκοποῦ to go aside from the mark, (Plato Philosophus) 8. to deviate from the course, to be liable to deviation , (Plato Philosophus); λόγοι παραλλάσσοντες delirious , (Euripides) 9. to slip aside or away , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

παραλυσις.definition: a loosening by the side: paralysis, palsy , (Theophrastus Philosophus) (ML)

παραναλισκω.definition: to spend amiss, to waste, squander , (Demosthenes Orator):—;Pass., of persons, to be sacrificed uselessly , 3rd plural aor1 παραναλώθησαν (Plutarch) (ML)

παρανομος.definition: 1. acting contrary to law, lawless , (Euripides) 2. of things, contrary to law, unlawful , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.:—; adverb , παρανόμως, illegally , (Thucydides) 3. in attic law, παράνομα γράφειν, εἰπεῖν to propose an illegal measure , (Demosthenes Orator); παρανόμων γράφεσθαί τινα to indict one for proposing such a measure , (Demosthenes Orator): the indictment itself was παρανόμων γραφή (Aeschines Orator):—;in superlative , παρανομώτατα γεγραφότα (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

παραξιφις.definition: a knife worn beside the sword, a dirk , (Strabo Geographus) (ML)

παραπαν.definition: 1. altogether, absolutely , generally with Art., τὸ π. (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;with a negative , τὸ π. οὐδέν not at all , (Herdotus Historicus); οὔκ εἰμι τὸ π. ἄθεος (Plato Philosophus) 2. in reckoning, ἐπὶ διηκόσια τὸ παράπαν up to two hundred altogether , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

παραπετασμα.definition: that which is spread before a thing, a hanging curtain , (Herdotus Historicus):—; metaphorically a screen, cover , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

παραπτωσις.definition: a falling beside; κατὰ τὴν π. τινος in the course of an action, (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

παραρριπτω.definition: to throw beside : metaphorically to run the risk of doing a thing, with participle , π. λαμβάνων (Sophocles Tragicus): to throw aside, reject , [ variant dates Anthology Palantina (ML)

παρασιωπαω.definition: to pass over in silence , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

παραστασις.definition: 1. a putting aside or away, banishing, relegatio , (Plato Philosophus), etc. 2. a setting out things for sale, retail-trade , (Aristotle Philosopher) 3. παρίσταμαι); intransitive a being beside : 4. a position or post near a king, (Xenophon Historicus) 5. presence of mind, courage , (Polybius Historicus): also, desperation , (Polybius Historicus) 6. as law-term, a small money deposit on entering law-suits, (Isaeus Orator) (ML)

παραταξις.definition: 1. a placing in line of battle , ἐκ παρατάξεως in regular battle , (Thucydides), etc. 2. of marshalling a political party, arrangement , (Aeschines Orator) from παρατάσσω (ML)

παρατασσω.definition: 1. to place side by side, draw up in battle-order , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;Mid. to draw up one's men in battle-order , (Xenophon Historicus); so of ships, (Thucydides):—;Mid. and Pass. to be drawn up along , παρατετάχατο παρὰ τὴν ἀκτήν (Herdotus Historicus); ἑκατέρωθεν παρατεταγμένοι (Thucydides); so, παρετάξαντο ἀλλήλοις (Xenophon Historicus): absolute , παρατεταγμένοι or παραταξάμενοι in order of battle , (Thucydides) 2. in Mid. and Pass., also, to stand prepared , παρατετάχθαι πρὸς τὸ ἀποκρίνεσθαι (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

παρατρεχω.definition: 1. to run by or past , (Iliad by Homer) 2. to outrun, overtake , (Iliad by Homer): π. τὰ τότε κακά to go beyond, exceed them, (Euripides) 3. to run through or over, run across (a space of ground expressed or implied), (Xenophon Historicus) 4. to run over , i. e. treat in a cursory way , (Isocrates Orator):—; to slight, neglect , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 5. to escape unnoticed , τινά (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

παρεδρευω.definition: 1. to sit constantly beside, attend constantly, be always near , Lat. assidere , with dative , (Euripides) 2. of judges, to be an assessor , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

παρεκτεινω.definition: to stretch out in line , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

παρεξ.definition: 1. as preposition , 2. with genitive loci, outside, before , παρὲκ λιμένος (Odyssey by Homer); παρὲξ ὁδοῦ out of the road, (Iliad by Homer) 3. like χωρίς, besides, except, exclusive of , παρὲξ τοῦ ἀργύρου (Herdotus Historicus) 4. with accusative out by the side of, along side of , παρὲξ ἅλα (Iliad by Homer); παρὲξ τὴν νῆσον away from the island, (Odyssey by Homer); παρὲξ δοῦρα out of the way of spears, (Odyssey by Homer); παρὲκ νόον out of sense and reason, foolishly, (Iliad by Homer); παρὲξ Ἀχιλῆα without the knowledge of Achilles, (Iliad by Homer) 5. as adverb , 6. of Place, out beside , στῆ δὲ παρέξ hard by , (Iliad by Homer); νῆχε παρέξ was swimming out along shore , (Odyssey by Homer) 7. metaphorically beside the mark , παρὲξ ἀγορεύειν (Iliad by Homer) 8. ἄλλα παρὲξ μεμνώμεθα let us talk of something else , (Odyssey by Homer); παρὲξ ἢ ὅσον except so long as, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

παρθενια.definition: marks of virginity; tokens of virginity

παριστανω.definition: παρ-ιστάνω , see: παρίστημι. παρ-ίστημι [in LXX for עָמַד, etc. ;] __I. Transitive verb. in present tense., imperfect., future tense., 1 aorist.; __1. to place beside, present, provide : with accusative, , , ; with accusative and dative, , , , ; before accusative pred., (late pres., παριστάνετε), , , , , . __2. to present to the mind (cl.) : by argument, to prove (Xen., FlJ, al.), with accusative, __II. Intransitive. in perfect., pluperfect., 2 aorist.; __1. to stand by or beside one : with dative of person(s), ; ptcp., . __2. to appear : with nom. pred., before ἐνώπιον, with dative of person(s), so fut. mid. (of. LS, see word, B, ii, 2), __3. to be at hand, be present, have come : (LXX); of servants in attendance, ἐνώπιον τ. θεοῦ, absol., οἱ παρεστῶτες, before αὐτῷ, , 4; of time, __4. to stand by for help or defence (Hom., Dem., Xen., al.): with dative of person(s), , .† (AS)

παροδευω.definition: 1. to pass by , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 2. with accusative to go past , (Lucian) (ML)

παροινεω.definition: 1. to behave ill at wine, play drunken tricks , (Isaeus Orator) 2. to act like a drunken man , (Plutarch); παροινήσας in a drunken fit , (Plato Philosophus) 3. transitive to treat with drunken violence :—; Pass. to be so treated , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

παροραω.definition: 1. to look at by the way, notice, remark , (Xenophon Historicus); τί τινι something in one, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. to overlook, disregard, neglect , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. 3. to see amiss, see wrong , (Plato Philosophus) 4. to look sideways , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

πασσαλος.definition: 1. a peg on which to hang clothes, arms, etc., (Homer), etc.; ἀπὸ πασσαλόφι ζυγὸν ᾕρεον (Iliad by Homer); ἀπὸ πασσάλου αἴνυτο τόξον (Odyssey by Homer); ἐκ πασσαλόφι κρέμασεν φόρμιγγα (Odyssey by Homer) 2. a gag , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

πασσω.definition: 1. to sprinkle , φάρμακα πάσσων laying salves upon a wound, (Iliad by Homer): —;with genitive partitive , πάσσε ἁλός sprinkle some salt, (Iliad by Homer) 2. to besprinkle , χρυσῶι, ῥόδοις π. τινά (Aristophanes Comicus) 3. metaphorically to embroider, broider , (Iliad by Homer); π. ἀέθλους to work battles in embroidery , (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

πατριος.definition: 1. of or belonging to one's father , Lat. patrius , (Pindar), etc. 2. = πατρικός, derived from one's fathers, hereditary , οἱπ. θεοί (Herdotus Historicus), etc.: —; τὰ πάτρια, Lat. instituta majorum , κατὰ τὰ πάτρια (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.; rarely in singular , τὸ πάτριον παρείς neglecting the rule of our fathers , (Thucydides) Cf. πατρῷος. (ML)

παχνη.definition: hoar-frost, rime , Lat. pruina , (Odyssey by Homer): metaphorically , κουροβόρος π. the clotted blood of the eaten children, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

παχος.definition: 1. thickness , (Odyssey by Homer):—; absolute , πάχος in thickness , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. π. σαρκός stoutness , (Euripides) (ML)

παχυς.definition: 1. thick, stout , (Homer):—; later, stout, fat , (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. of things, thick, massive , (Homer):—; adverb -έως, roughly , of stating or arguing, (Aristotle Philosopher); παχύτερον or -έρως, (Plato Philosophus) 3. of liquids, thick, curdled, clotted , (Iliad by Homer) 4. οἱ παχέες the men of substance, the wealthy class , (Herdotus Historicus); τοὺς παχεῖς καὶ πλουσίους (Aristophanes Comicus) 5. in [ variant dates Comica Adespota and Prose, thick-witted, gross, dull, stupid , like Lat. pinguis, crassus , [ variant dates Comica Adespota 6. comparative παχύτερος, sup. -ύτατος:—;irregular comparative πάσσων, ον, (Odyssey by Homer):—;Sup. πάχιστος, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

πεδαω.definition: 1. to bind with fetters, to bind fast, make fast , (Odyssey by Homer) 2. to shackle, trammel, constrain , (Homer); with infinitive to constrain one to do a thing, (Homer) (ML)

πεδιον.definition: a plain or flat , and collectively a plain flat open country , (Homer), etc. (ML)

πεζος.definition: 1. on foot , πεζοί fighters on foot , opposite to horsemen, (Homer):—;also on land, going by land , opposite to sea-faring, (Homer):—;so, ὁ πεζὸς στρατός, or ὁ πεζός alone, sometimes foot-soldiery, infantry , opposite to cavalry ἡ ἵππος); (Herdotus Historicus) 2. ὁ πεζός, also, a land-force or army , opposite to a naval force, (Herdotus Historicus); so, τὸ πεζόν (Herdotus Historicus); στρατιὰ καὶ ναυτικὴ καὶ πεζή (Thucydides); τὰ πεζὰ κράτιστοι strongest by land , (Thucydides) 3. of animals, land , as opposite to birds and fishes, τὰ π. καὶ τὰ πτηνά beasts and birds, (Plato Philosophus) 4. metaphorically of language, not rising above the ground, prosaic , (Lucian) 5. dative feminine πεζῇ (entry ὁδῷ); as adverb , on foot , (Xenophon Historicus) 6. by land , (Thucydides) (ML)

πειρατηριον.definition: 1. φόνια πειρατήρια the murderous ordeal , (Euripides) 2. a pirate's nest , (Strabo Geographus) from πειρα_τής (ML)

πειρατης.definition: a pirate , Lat. pirata , i. e. one who attacks ships, (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

πελας.definition: 1. near, hard by, close , with genitive , (Odyssey by Homer) 3. absolute , χριμφθεὶς πέλας (Odyssey by Homer); π. στείχειν, παρεῖναι, στῆναι [ variant dates Tragica Adespota 4. οἱ πέλας (i.e. ὄντες); one's neighbours , (Thucydides), etc.: hence one's fellow-creatures, all men , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

πελεκαω.definition: to hew or shape with an axe , Lat. dolare , (Odyssey by Homer) (in epic aor1 πελέκκησε), (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

πελεκυς.definition: 1. an axe for felling trees, with two edges, opposite to the ἡμιπέλεκκον, (Homer) 2. a sacrificial axe , (Homer)—;That it was not, properly, a battle axe appears from the phrase, οὐ δόρασι μάχεσθαι, ἀλλὰ καὶ πελέκεσι to fight not with spears only, but with common axes , i. e. to the last, (Herdotus Historicus) 3. in (Theophrastus Philosophus) Char., πέλεκυς as a child's nickname seems to mean a sharp blade. (ML)

πελταστης.definition: one who bears a light shield πέλτη); instead of the heavy ὅπλον, a targeteer , Lat. cetratus , (Euripides), etc. The peltasts held a place between the ὁπλῖται and ψιλοί. (ML)

πελτη.definition: 1. a small light shield of leather without a rim ἴτυς); a target , Lat. cetra , originally used by the Thracians, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 2. a body of πελτασταί, (Euripides) 3. a horse's ornament , (Euripides) 4. = παλτόν, a shaft, pole , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

πελυξ.definition: a kind of axe , (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor) (ML)

πεμμα.definition: any kind of dressed food; but mostly in plural , pastry, cakes, sweetmeats , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

πενθικος.definition: of or for mourning, mournful :—; adverb , πενθικῶς ἔχειν τινός to be in mourning for a person, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

πενομαι.definition: 1. Dep., used in present and imperfect : 2. intransitive to work for one's daily bread ; generally, to toil, work, labour , (Homer) 3. to be poor or needy , Solon , (Euripides), etc. 4. with genitive to be poor in, have need of , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 5. transitive to work at, prepare, get ready , δαῖτα πένοντο (Odyssey by Homer); τί σε χρὴ ταῦτα πένεσθα; (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

πενταετης.definition: 1. five years old , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. of Time, lasting five years , (Thucydides):—; neuter adverb πεντάετες, for five years , (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

πενταπηχυς.definition: five cubits long or broad , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

πεντηκονταρχος.definition: the commander of fifty men , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

πεντηκοστος.definition: 1. fiftieth , (Plato Philosophus) 2. as Substantive , ἡ πεντηκοστή, 3. (i.e. μερίς); at Athens the duty of one-fiftieth , or two per century , on all exports and imports, (Isaeus Orator); εὕρηκε καινὴν ἱππικῆς τινὰ πεντηκοστήν he invented a new two per century duty , in lieu of his cavalry service, i. e. paid this instead of it, (Demosthenes Orator) 4. (i.e. ἡμέρα); the fiftieth day (after the Passover), Pentecost , (New Testament) (ML)

πεπειρος.definition: 1. ripe , Lat. maturus , [ variant dates Anthology Palantina 2. metaphorically softened , ὀργή (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

πεπων.definition: 1. of fruit, cooked by the sun, ripe, mellow , Lat. mitis , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 2. metaphorically in vocative , mostly as a term of endearment, kind, gentle , ὦ πέπον my good friend , (Iliad by Homer); κριὲ πέπον my pet ram, (Odyssey by Homer);—; in bad sense, soft, weak , (Iliad by Homer); ὦ πέπονες ye weaklings , (Iliad by Homer): —; μόχθος πέπων softened pain, (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.: with dative , ἐχθροῖς π. gentle to one's foes, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

περαινω.definition: 1. to bring to an end, finish, accomplish, execute , [ variant dates Tragica Adespota , etc.:—;Pass. to be brought to an end, be finished , πάντα πεπείρανται (Odyssey by Homer): to be fulfilled, accomplished , (Euripides) etc. 2. in speaking, to end a discourse, finish speaking, (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc. 3. to repeat from beginning to end , (Aristophanes Comicus):—; to relate , (Euripides) 4. absolute to effect one's purpose , especially with a negative , οὐδὲν π. to come to no issue, do no good, make no progress , (Euripides) 5. intransitive to make way, reach or penetrate , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 6. intransitive to come to an end, end , (Plutarch) (ML)

περιβλεπτος.definition: looked at from all sides, admired of all observers , (Euripides) (ML)
