συγκρισις.definition: 1. a compounding , (Plato Philosophus), etc. 2. a comparing, comparison , (Aristotle Philosopher), etc. (ML)

συγκροτεω.definition: 1. to strike together; ς. τὼ χεῖρε to clap the hands for joy, (Xenophon Historicus); but also to smite them together in grief, (Lucian):—;Pass. to be applauded , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. to hammer or weld together , (Aristophanes Comicus): hence, to weld a number of men into one body, i. e. organise them, (Demosthenes Orator), etc.:—; perfect passive participle συγκεκροτημένος well-trained, in good discipline , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

συγκυρεω.definition: 1. to come together by chance , (Iliad by Homer): to meet with an accident, συγκύρσαι τύχῃ (Sophocles Tragicus); εἰς ἓν μοίρας ξυνέκυρσας art involved in one and the same fate, (Euripides) 2. with participle , like τυγχάνω, συνεκύρησε παραπεσοῦσα νηῦς fell in the way by chance , (Herdotus Historicus) 3. of events and accidents, like συμβαίνω, to happen, occur , (Herdotus Historicus): —; impersonal , with infinitive , συνεκύρησε γενέσθαι it came to pass that . ., (Herdotus Historicus):—;so, in Pass., τὸ ἐς Λακεδαιμονίους συγκεκυρημένον (Herdotus Historicus) 4. of places, to be contiguous to , τινί (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

συκαμινον.definition: the fruit of the συκάμινος, a mulberry , Lat. morum , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

συκοφαντης.definition: a false accuser, slanderer , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.; (never used in the modern sense of sycophant , i. e. κόλαξ); generally, a false adviser , (Demosthenes Orator) (Commonly derived from σῦκον, φαίνω, one who informed against persons exporting figs from Attica: better perhaps a fig-shewer , i. e. one who brings figs to light by shaking the tree (the figs having been hidden in the thick foliage); and then, metaphorically , one who makes rich men yield up their fruit by false accusations). (ML)

συκοφαντια.definition: 1. false accusation, slander, calumny , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. 2. a sophism , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

συλληψις.definition: 1. a taking together: a seizing, arresting , ποιεῖσθαι ξύλληψιν to arrest , (Thucydides) 2. conception , (Plutarch) (ML)

συλλογη.definition: 1. a gathering, collecting , (Thucydides): metaphorically , ἐν γενείου ξυλλογῇ τριχώματος in the first harvest of a beard, i. e. in early manhood, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. a levying of soldiers, Lat. conscriptio , (Xenophon Historicus) 3. a summary, recapitulation , (Demosthenes Orator) 4. (from Pass.) an assembly, meeting , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

συλλογισμος.definition: 1. computation , (Plato Philosophus) 2. a conclusion, inference from premisses , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

συμβολη.definition: 1. a coming together, meeting, joining , (Xenophon Historicus): the juncture of two parts, the end , Lat. commissura , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. in hostile sense, an encounter, engagement, battle , (Herdotus Historicus) 3. = συμβόλαιον II, a contract, covenant , (Aristotle Philosopher); in (Aristophanes Comicus) Ach. there is a play on signfs. II and III, encounter and accounts, charge and charges. 4. in plural , συμβολαί were contributions for a common meal, πίνειν ἀπὸ συμβολῶν, like de symbolis(Terentius Grammaticus Latinus) entertainment itself, a picnic , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

συμβολον.definition: 1. a sign or token by which one infers a thing, [ variant dates Tragica Adespota ; λαμπάδος τὸ σύμβολον the token of the beacon-fire, (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;often in plural , of marks on the body, (Euripides); of omens , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. a pledge or pawn , on which money was advanced, (Lysias Orator) 3. in plural tallies , Lat. tesserae hospitales , i.e. the halves of a bone or coin, which two persons broke between them, each keeping one piece, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 4. at Athens, a ticket, counter , Lat. tessera , such as were given to the dicasts, on presenting which they received their fee, (Demosthenes Orator) 5. a permit or licence to reside, given to aliens , (Aristophanes Comicus); a ticket given by each person who joined in a picnic, to be presented for payment at the end (compare συμβολή IV), (Aristophanes Comicus) 6. in Eccl. the distinctive mark of Christians, a confession of faith, a creed , Lat. symbolum . 7. in legal phrase, σύμβολα were covenants between two states for protection of commerce , (Demosthenes Orator), etc.; σύμβολα ποιεῖσθαι πρὸς πόλιν to make a commercial treaty with a state, τὰ ς. συγχέειν to violate such treaty , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

συμβουλια.definition: advice or counsel given , (Herdotus Historicus); in plural counsels , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

συμμαχεω.definition: to be an ally, to be in alliance , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;generally, to help, aid, succour , τινί (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.:—;Pass. to be assisted , (Lucian) (ML)

συμμαχια.definition: 1. an alliance offensive and defensive (opposite to an ἐπιμαχία, defensive) , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.: συμμαχίαν ποιεῖσθαι πρός τινα (Herdotus Historicus); τινί (Thucydides) 2. generally, the duty of an ally , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. = τὸ συμμαχικόν, the body of allies , (Herdotus Historicus): also, the country of one's allies , (Thucydides) 4. an allied or auxiliary force , (Thucydides) (ML)

συμμετρος.definition: 1. commensurate with another thing, (Euripides): exactly fitting , (Aeschulus Tragicus); τῷδε τἀνδρὶ ξ. being of like age with , (Sophocles Tragicus); ποίᾳ σύμμετρος τύχ; coincident with what chance? i. e. in the very nick of time, (Sophocles Tragicus); see. infr. III. 2. 2. commensurable , (Aristotle Philosopher) 3. in measure with, proportionable, exactly suitable , (Isocrates Orator), etc. 4. absolute in right measure, in due proportion, symmetrical , opposite to ὑπερβάλλων and ἐλλείπων, (Plato Philosophus), etc. 5. generally, fitting, meet, due , (Aeschulus Tragicus);—; σύμμετρος ὡς κλύειν within fit distance for hearing, (Sophocles Tragicus) 6. adverb -τρως, (Isocrates Orator), etc. 7. in due time , (Euripides) (ML)

συμμιγης.definition: 1. commingled, promiscuous , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc. 2. with dative commingled with , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

συμμιγνυμι.definition: 1. to mix together, commingle , (Homeric Hymns); to mix one thing with another, τί τινι (Herdotus Historicus), attic; with accusative only, συμμίξαντες τὰ στρατόπεδα having combined them, (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass., of a river, to be mingled with another river, with dative , (Iliad by Homer): to join forces , of two armies, (Thucydides):—; metaphorically , οὐδείς [ ἐστι] τῷ κακὸν οὐ συνεμίχθη there is none who has not misery as an ingredient in his nature , (Herdotus Historicus); συμμιγέντων τούτων πάντων when all these things happened together , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. to unite , θεοὺς γυναιξί (Homeric Hymns):—;Pass. to have intercourse with , with dative , (Herdotus Historicus) 3. metaphorically , ς. τινὰ τύχᾳ to make him acquainted with fortune, (Pindar); πρῆγμα συμμῖξαί τινι to communicate a matter to another, (Herdotus Historicus) 4. intransitive in Act. to have intercourse with, to associate or communicate with others, with dative , (Theognis Elegiacus), etc.; ς. πρός τινα to join him, (Xenophon Historicus):—;generally, to meet for conversation or traffic , (Herdotus Historicus); ς. τινί to converse with , (Herdotus Historicus) 5. in hostile sense, to meet in close fight, come to blows, engage , τινί with one, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 6. generally, to meet , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

συμμικτος.definition: commingled, promiscuous , (Hesiod): especially of troops, irregular , (Herdotus Historicus) adverb -τως, (Strabo Geographus) (ML)

συμμιξις.definition: 1. commixture , τινος πρός τι (Plato Philosophus) 2. intercourse , (Plutarch) (ML)

συμπαριστημι.definition: 1. to place beside one also , (Pindar) 2. Pass., with aorist2 et perfect active , to stand beside, assist , τινι (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

συμπας.definition: 1. all together, all at once, all in a body , (Homer), attic; in attic, the Art. is often added in the case of Numerals, πέντ᾽ ἦσαν οἱ ξύμπαντες (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. with collective nouns, the whole , ὁ ς. στρατός (Herdotus Historicus); στρατὸς ς. (Sophocles Tragicus); ξύμπασα πόλις the state as a whole , (Thucydides); ξ. γνώμη the general scope (of a speech), (Thucydides) 3. τὸ σύμπαν the whole together, the sum of the matter, (Herdotus Historicus); τὸ ξύμπαν εἰπεῖν (Thucydides) 4. τὸ σύμπαν, as adverb altogether, on the whole, in general , (Thucydides), etc. (ML)

συμπατεω.definition: to tread together, trample under foot , (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor):—;Pass. to be trampled under foot , (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

συμπεραινω.definition: 1. to join or assist in accomplishing , (Euripides):—;Mid., συμπεραίνεσθαί τινι ἔχθραν to join fully in enmity with another, (Demosthenes Orator) 2. to decide or conclude absolutely , ς. φροντίδα to make up one's mind, (Euripides); κλῇθρα μοχλοῖς ς. to make the doors doubly sure by bars, (Euripides):—;Pass. to be quite finished , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

συμπεριφερω.definition: 1. to carry round along with or together , (Plato Philosophus) 2. Pass. to be carried round together , (Plato Philosophus) 3. συμπεριφέρεσθαί τινι to have intercourse with one, (Polybius Historicus): to adapt oneself to circumstances, with dative , (Aeschines Orator) 4. to be well acquainted with things, (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

συμπλεκω.definition: 1. to twine or plait together , (Plato Philosophus); τινί with a thing, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus); συμπλέκοντες τὼ χεῖρε εἰς τοὐπίσω joining their hands behind them, (Thucydides) 2. Pass. to be twined together, entwined, entangled , (Euripides); ἴχνη συμπεπλεγμένα tracks entangled, crossing in different directions , (Xenophon Historicus) 3. of persons wrestling, to be locked together with another, with dative , (Herdotus Historicus): generally, to be engaged in close fight , (Demosthenes Orator): of a ship, to be entangled with her opponent, (Herdotus Historicus):—;then, metaphorically to be entangled in , τῇ Σκυθῶν ἐρημίᾳ συμπλακῆναι (Aristophanes Comicus); συμπεπλέγμεθα ξένῳ we are entangled or engaged with him, (Euripides); of war, to be engaged in , (Demosthenes Orator) 4. intransitive in Act., = Pass., (Euripides) (ML)

συμποδιζω.definition: 1. to tie the feet together, bind hand and foot , (Aristophanes Comicus):—;Pass. to be entangled in a net , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. metaphorically to entangle , Lat. impedire , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

συμπολεμεω.definition: to join in war , (Thucydides), etc.; τινί with one, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

συμπροπεμπω.definition: to join in escorting , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; ς. τινὰ ναυσίν (Thucydides) (ML)

συμπτωμα.definition: a chance, casualty , (Aristotle Philosopher): in bad sense, a mishap, mischance , (Thucydides) (ML)

συμφρασσω.definition: 1. to press or pack closely together , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. absolute of troops, to close their ranks, form in close order , (Xenophon Historicus) 3. to block up, close , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

συμφυρω.definition: to knead together: beat black and blue , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus):—;Pass., (Euripides); ψυχὴ συμπέφυρται μετὰ τοῦ κακοῦ (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

συμψαω.definition: to sweep away , of a rapid river, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

συναδω.definition: 1. to sing with or together , (Aeschines Orator); ς. ᾠδάν (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. generally, to be in accord with , τινί (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. transitive to celebrate together , τινά (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

συναλλαγμα.definition: a mutual agreement, covenant, contract , (Demosthenes Orator), etc.: in plural dealings between men , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

συναπτω.definition: 1. to tie or bind together, to join together, unite , ς. χέρα, in sign of friendship, (Euripides); ἰδού, ξύναψον (i.e. τὴν χέρα); (Euripides); but, ς. χεῖρά τινος ἐν βρόχοις to bind it fast , (Euripides):—; ς. πόδα or ἴχνος τινί to meet him, (Euripides); ς. κῶλον τάφῳ to approach the grave, (Euripides); so, φόνος ς. τινὰ γᾷ (Euripides):—; ξ. βλέφαρα to close the eyes, (Euripides); ς. στόμα to kiss one, (Euripides):—; ς. κακὰ κακοῖς to link misery with misery, (Euripides); but, ς. κακόν τινι to link him with misery , (Euripides): ς. τινὶ δαῖτα to give one a meal, (Euripides): proverbial , ς. λίνον λίνῳ to join thread to thread, i. e. to compare things of the same sort, (Plato Philosophus) 2. to connect in thought, to combine , (Plato Philosophus): ς. μηχανήν to frame a plan, (Aeschulus Tragicus); ς. ὄναρ εἴς τινα to connect it with him, refer it to him, (Euripides); ξυνῆψε πάντας ἐς μίαν βλάβην involved them in one loss, (Euripides) 3. in hostile sense, ς. εἰς μάχην to bring into action, (Herdotus Historicus); ἐλπὶς πόλεις ξυνῆψε engaged them in conflict , (Euripides) 4. ς. μάχην to join battle, (Herdotus Historicus); τινί with one, (Aeschulus Tragicus); πρός τινα (Thucydides): also (without μάχην); to engage , (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass., νεῖκος συνῆπταί τινι πρός τινα (Herdotus Historicus) 5. in friendly sense, to unite , (Xenophon Historicus): —;Pass., συνάπτεσθαί τινι to have intercourse with , [ variant dates Anthology Palantina 6. with accusative rei, ς. μῦθον, ὅρκους (Euripides); ς.τινὶ γάμους, λέκτρα, κῆδος to form an alliance by marriage, (Euripides): ξυνάπτεσθαι κῆδος τῆς θυγατρός to get one's daughter married, (Thucydides) 7. intransitive : 8. in local sense, to border on, lie next to , (Herdotus Historicus); Τήνῳ συνάπτει Ἄνδρος (Aeschulus Tragicus) 9. of Time, to be nigh at hand , (Pindar); so of events, λύπη ς. τινί (Euripides) 10. metaphorically of thoughts, to meet together , (Aristotle Philosopher):—; to be connected with , πρός τι (Aristotle Philosopher) 11. of persons, ς. λόγοισι to enter into conversation, (Sophocles Tragicus); so, ἐς λόγους ξ. τινί (Euripides); also, ς. εἰς χορεύματα to join in the dance, (Euripides); ς. ἐς χεῖρα γῇ, i. e. to come close to land, (Euripides) 12. τύχα ποδὸς ξυνάπτει μοι, i. e. I have come in good time, (Euripides) 13. Mid. to be next to, connected with , τινι (Xenophon Historicus) 14. to take part with one, to assist , τινι (Euripides); absolute , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 15. to bring upon oneself , πληγάς (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

συναριθμεω.definition: to reckon in, to take into the account, enumerate , (Isaeus Orator); so in Mid., (Aeschines Orator):—;Pass. to be counted with others, to be taken into account , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

συνδειπνεω.definition: to dine or sup with another, with dative , (Xenophon Historicus); μετά τινων (Demosthenes Orator):—; absolute to dine or sup with others , (Xenophon Historicus), etc.; οἱ ξυνδειπνοῦντες the members of a picnic party , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

συνδυαζω.definition: 1. to join two and two, couple , (Aristotle Philosopher): —;Pass. to be coupled with something else , (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. in Pass. to be coupled, to pair , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

συνεγγυς.definition: 1. of Place, near together , (Thucydides), etc.; ς. ἀλλήλων or ἀλλήλοις (Aristotle Philosopher):—; τὸ ς. nearness, proximity , (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. of Time, (Aristotle Philosopher) 3. of Quality, οἱ ς. persons of similar rank , (Aristotle Philosopher); ἡ ς. αἰτία the proximate cause, (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

συνεκτρεφω.definition: to rear up along with or together , (Plato Philosophus):—;Pass. to grow up with , τινί (Euripides) (ML)

συνελκω.definition: 1. to draw together, to draw up, contract , (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. to draw out along with, to help to draw out , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

συνεξαιρω.definition: to assist in raising : Pass., aor1 participle συνεξαρθείς being lifted up at once , (Plutarch); being excited at the same time , (Lucian) (ML)

συνεξερχομαι.definition: Dep.:—; to go or come out with , τινι (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

συνεπισταμαι.definition: Dep. to be privy to , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

συνεπιτιθημι.gloss: to join in making an attack
συνεπιτιθημι.definition: 1. to help in putting on , (Plutarch) 2. Mid. to join in attacking , τινι (Thucydides); ξ. τῷ ἔργῳ ̀ 6 6̀ το fall to the work together , (Thucydides) (ML)

συνηλιξ.definition: of like or equal age , Lat. aequalis , a playmate, comrade, [ 6th/5th c.BC , variant dates Anthology Palantina (ML)

συνθεσις.definition: 1. a putting together, composition, combination , (Plato Philosophus); γραμμάτων συνθέσεις, i. e. syllables and words, (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;also, of an author's composition , (Isocrates Orator) 2. metaphorically , like συνθεσία, an agreement, treaty , (Pindar) 3. Lat. synthesis was a suit of clothes , (Martialis Epigrammaticus Latinus); especially a loose gown , worn at dinner-parties, (Martialis Epigrammaticus Latinus) (ML)

συνθετος.definition: 1. put together, composite, compound , (Plato Philosophus): complex , (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. put together, fictitious , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. metaphorically agreed upon , ἐκ συνθέτου by agreement , Lat. ex composito , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

συνθηκη.definition: 1. a composition , of words and sentences, (Lucian) 2. a conventional agreement, convention, compact , (Plato Philosophus); ἐκ συνθήκης, ex composito, by agreement , (Plato Philosophus); κατὰ συνθήκην conventionally , (Aristotle Philosopher) 3. the article of a compact or treaty , (Thucydides):—;mostly in plural the articles of agreement , and collectively, a contract, compact, covenant, treaty , (Herdotus Historicus), attic; συνθήκας ποιέεσθαί τινι (Herdotus Historicus); ἐκ τῶν συνθηκῶν according to the covenant , (Isocrates Orator); κατὰ τὰς ς. (Thucydides) (ML)

συνιστωρ.definition: 1. knowing along with another, conscious , ὡς θεοὶ ξυνίστορες as the gods are witnesses , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc. 2. with accusative (with the verbal construction), πολλὰ συνίστορα κακά conscious of many evils, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

συνοικιζω.definition: 1. to make to live with , (Isocrates Orator); ς. τινὶ τὴν θυγατέρα to give him one's daughter in marriage , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. to combine in one city, unite under a capital or metropolis , ξ. πάντας (i.e. ἐς τὰς Ἀθήνας)) (Thucydides):—;Pass., ξυνοικισθείσης πόλεως the city having been regularly formed , opposite to κατὰ κώμας οἰκίζεσθαι, (Thucydides) 3. to join in peopling or colonising a country, (Euripides) 4. generally to unite, associate , (Plutarch) (ML)

συνταγμα.definition: 1. that which is put together in order : 2. a body of troops, squadron, contingent , (Xenophon Historicus) 3. the constitution of a state , ς. πολιτείας a form of constitution, (Isocrates Orator) 4. an arrangement of musical notes , (Aristotle Philosopher) 5. a regular collection of writings, a work, book, doctrine , (Plutarch) 6. = σύνταξις II. 3, (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

συνταξις.definition: 1. a putting together, arranging, arrangement, organisation, order , (Thucydides): rule , (Demosthenes Orator) 2. a systematic treatise , (Aristotle Philosopher): a narrative , (Polybius Historicus) 3. grammatical construction, syntax , (Lucian) 4. a body of troops , ἡ εἰς μυρίους ς. their contingent towards 10, 000, (Xenophon Historicus) 5. a covenant, contract , (Demosthenes Orator) 6. an assigned impost, contribution , (Demosthenes Orator) 7. a payment, allowance, pension , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

συνταρασσω.definition: to throw all together into confusion, to confound, disturb, trouble , Lat. conturbare , (Iliad by Homer), attic:—;Pass., αἰθὴρ πόντῳ ξυντετάρακται air is confounded with sea, (Aeschulus Tragicus): to be thrown into confusion , of soldiers, (Thucydides); of social order, (Sophocles Tragicus); metaphorically of persons, to be confounded, greatly troubled, much distressed , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

συνυφαινω.definition: to weave together : metaphorically to frame with art, devise cunningly , (Odyssey by Homer):—;Pass., ὥστε ταῦτα συνυφανθῆναι so that this web was woven , i. e. this business undertaken, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

συριγξ.definition: 1. a pipe : 2. a musical pipe, a shepherd's pipe, Panspipe , (Iliad by Homer), attic 3. anything like a pipe : 4. a spear-case , = δορατοθήκη, (Iliad by Homer) 5. the hole in the nave of a wheel , [ variant dates Tragica Adespota 6. a duct or channel in the body, in plural the nostrils , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

συριζω.definition: 1. to play the σῦριγξ, to pipe , (Euripides); with accusative cognate , συρίζων ὑμεναίους (Euripides) 2. to whistle, hiss , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;with accusative cognate , συρίζων φόνον hissing forth murder, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. to hiss an actor, Lat. explodere , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

συρραπτω.definition: to sew or stitch together, sew up , Lat. consuo , (Hesiod) (ML)

συσκηνος.definition: one who lives in the same tent, a messmate , Lat. contubernalis , (Thucydides) (ML)

συσκιαζω.definition: 1. to shade quite over, throw a shade over, shade closely or thickly , (Hesiod); γένυν ς., i. e.to get a beard, (Euripides): metaphorically , συσκηνῶσαι τὰς ἁμαρτίας (Demosthenes Orator) 2. intransitive to be thick-shaded , (Euripides) (ML)

συσκιος.definition: closely shaded, thickly shaded , (Xenophon Historicus); σύσκιόν τι a closely-shaded place , (Lucian) (ML)

συσκοταζω.definition: to grow quite dark : impersonal , συσκοτάζει it grows dark , (Thucydides) (ML)

συσπαω.definition: 1. to draw together, draw up, contract , (Plato Philosophus) 2. to draw together by stitching, sew together , (Xenophon Historicus) 3. in Mid. to draw along with one , (Plutarch) (ML)

συστασις.definition: 1. a putting together, composition , (Aristotle Philosopher); ς. προσώπου a studied expression of countenance, of Pericles, (Plutarch) 2. a bringing together, introduction, recommendation , (Polybius Historicus) 3. συνίσταμαι); a standing together, meeting : in hostile sense, close combat, conflict , (Herdotus Historicus); metaphorically , ς. γνώμης a conflict of mind, intense anxiety, (Thucydides) 4. a meeting, a knot of men , (Euripides); κατὰ ξυστάσεις γιγνόμενοι forming into knots , (Thucydides): a political union , (Demosthenes Orator) 5. friendship or alliance , (Polybius Historicus): a conspiracy , (Plutarch) 6. construction, structure, constitution , (Plato Philosophus): absolute a political constitution , (Plato Philosophus) 7. metaphorically of the mind, ς. φρενῶν contraction, sternness, sullenness , (Euripides) (ML)

συστρεμμα.definition: anything twisted up together: a body of men, a crowd, concourse , (Polybius Historicus) from συστρέφω (ML)

σφακελιζω.definition: to be gangrened , ἐσφακέλισε τὸ ὀστέον (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

σφαλερος.definition: 1. likely to make one stumble or trip : metaphorically slippery, perilous, dangerous , Lat. lubricus , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—; σφαλερόν [ ἐστι], with infinitive , it is dangerous to . ., (Plato Philosophus), etc. 2. σφάλλομαι); ready to fall, tottering, reeling, staggering , (Aeschulus Tragicus); σφ. σύμμαχοι (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

σφαλλω.definition: 1. Lat. fall-o (the sigma being lost):—; to make to fall, throw down, overthrow , properly by tripping up, to trip up in wrestling , (Homer), etc.; σφ. ναῦς to throw her on her beam-ends , (Plutarch); ἵππος σφ. τὸν ἀναβάτην throws him, (Xenophon Historicus):—;Pass. to be tripped up , (Aristophanes Comicus); of a drunken man, σφαλλόμενος reeling, staggering , (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. generally, to cause to fall, overthrow, defeat , (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass. to be overthrown, to fall, fail, be undone, become helpless , (Herdotus Historicus), attic; τόδ᾽ ἐσφάλη this mishap took place , (Sophocles Tragicus); οὔ τι μὴ σφαλῶ γ᾽ ἐν σοί I shall not fail in thy business, (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. to baffle, foil, balk, disappoint , (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass. to err, go wrong, be mistaken , (Herdotus Historicus) 4. the Pass. is also used with genitive rei, to be balked of or foiled in a thing, ἦ καὶ πατήρ τι σφάλλεται βουλευμάτω; (Aeschulus Tragicus); σφάλλεσθαι γάμου (Euripides); τῆς δόξης (Thucydides) (ML)

σφενδοναω.definition: 1. to sling, to use the sling , (Thucydides) 2. to strike by slinging , (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor) 3. to throw as from a sling :—;Pass., (Euripides) 4. to move like a swing, to swing to and fro , (Euripides) from σφενδόνη (ML)

σφενδονη.definition: 1. Lat. funda (the ς being lost), a sling , (Iliad by Homer): metaphorically , σφενδόνας ἀπ᾽ εὐμέτρου with well-measured throw, as from a sling , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. the hoop of a ring in which the stone was set as in a sling, especially the broader part round the stone , as in Lat. funda for pala annuli , (Euripides) 3. the stone or bullet of the sling , (Xenophon Historicus); τοιαύταις σφ., of hailstones, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

σφιγγω.definition: to bind tight, bind fast , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;Pass., (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

σφοδρος.definition: 1. vehement, violent, excessive , (Thucydides), etc. 2. of men, violent, impetuous , (Plato Philosophus): also strong, robust , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

σφονδυλος.definition: 1. a vertebra , (Aristophanes Comicus):—;in plural the backbone, spine , or the neck , (Euripides) 2. Lat. verticillus , the round weight attached to a spindle, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

σφυρα.definition: 1. a hammer , (Odyssey by Homer) 2. a beetle, mallet , for breaking clods of earth, (Hesiod) (ML)

σχαζω.definition: 1. properly to let loose : hence to slit, open , (Aristophanes Comicus); σχ. φλέβα to open a vein, (Xenophon Historicus), etc.:—;of flowers, σχ. κάλυκας [ variant dates Anthology Palantina 2. to let fall, drop , (Xenophon Historicus) 3. to let go , σχάσας τὴν φροντίδα having let the mind go, given it play , (Aristophanes Comicus); σχ. τὰς μηχανάς to let off the engines, (Plutarch) 4. to check, stop, stay , Lat. inhibere , κώπαν σχάσον, i. e. cease rowing, (Pindar); σχάσον ὄμμα lower thine eyes, (Euripides):—;Mid., σχασάμενος τὴν ἱππικήν having dropt one's horsemanship, "given up the turf," (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

σχεδια.definition: 1. a raft, float (such as was made off-hand , compare σχέδιος II), (Odyssey by Homer); generally, a boat, ship , (Euripides) 2. a bridge of boats , of the bridge of Xerxes, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

σχιζα.definition: 1. a piece of wood cleft off, a lath, splinter , Lat. scindula , (Odyssey by Homer): in plural cleft wood, fire-wood , (Homer) 2. an arrow , [ variant dates Anthology Palantina (ML)

σχοινισμα.definition: a measured out line; a piece of measured out land

σχοινισμος.gloss: a piece of measured out land
σχοινισμος.definition: a fencing with ropes : in plural roping, rope-fences , (Plutarch) (ML)

σχοινος.definition: 1. a rush , Lat. juncus, scirpus , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 2. a reed , used as an arrow or javelin , (Batrachomyomachia) 3. a place where rushes grow, a rushbed , (Odyssey by Homer) 4. a rush-rope , and generally, a rope, cord , (Oracle quoted in Herdotus Historicus) 5. a fence round a garden, [ variant dates Anthology Palantina 6. a land-measure , = 2 Persian parasangs, = 60 stades, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

σχολαστης.definition: 1. one who lives at ease , (Plutarch) 2. as adjective leisurely, idle , βίος (Plutarch) (ML)

σωματοποιεω.definition: 1. to make into a body, to consolidate, organise , (Polybius Historicus) 2. to provide with bodily strength, to recruit , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

σωρος.definition: 1. a heap , Lat. acervus , (Hesiod), etc. 2. generally, a heap, quantity , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

ταινια.definition: 1. a band, riband, fillet , especially a head-band , worn in sign of victory, (Xenophon Historicus), etc. 2. a strip or tongue of land , (Plutarch), etc. (ML)

τακτικος.definition: fit for ordering or arranging , especially in war, τ. ἀνήρ a tactician , (Xenophon Historicus); τακτικὸν ἡγεῖσθαί τι to think it a good piece of tactics , (Xenophon Historicus); οἱ τ. ἀριθμοί the regular battalions, (Xenophon Historicus): τὰ τακτικά the art of drawing up soldiers in array, tactics , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

ταλας.definition: suffering, wretched , Lat. miser , (Odyssey by Homer); ὦ τάλαιν᾽ ἐγώ (Aeschulus Tragicus); ὦ τάλαν (Sophocles Tragicus);—;with genitive causae, τάλαιν᾽ ἐγὼ τῆς ὕβρεως wretched that I am for this insolence, (Aristophanes Comicus):—;in bad sense, τάλαν wretch! (Odyssey by Homer)—; comparative τᾶλάντερος, η, ον: Sup. τᾶλάντατος, η, ον, (Aristophanes Comicus) τᾶλα_; doric also τᾶλᾶς: vocative τάλᾶν. (ML)

ταμιας.definition: 1. one who carves and distributes, a dispenser , (Iliad by Homer):—;of Zeus, as the dispenser of all things to men, (Iliad by Homer); so Aeolus is τ. ἀνέμων (Odyssey by Homer):—;of kings or rulers, a controller, director , (Pindar); τ. κώμων master of the revels, (Pindar); τ. Διός the priest of Zeus, (Pindar): τ. Μοισᾶν, i. e. a poet, (Pindar); οἶκος τ. στεφάνων that hath store of crowns, (Pindar); τῆς τε ἐπιθυμίας καὶ τῆς τύχης τ. controller both of his desire and of fortune, (Thucydides); τ. τριαίνης, of Poseidon, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. in Prose, a controller of payments, treasurer , (Herdotus Historicus); τ. τοῦ ἱροῦ the controller of the sacred treasure in the citadel of Athens, (Herdotus Historicus) 3. at Rome, the quaestor , (Plutarch) (ML)

ταμιευω.definition: 1. to be controller of receipts and expenditure, to be treasurer, paymaster , (Aristophanes Comicus):—;with genitive , τ. τῆς Παράλου to be paymaster of the Paralus, (Demosthenes Orator) 2. at Rome, to be quaestor , (Plutarch) 3. transitive to deal out, dispense , (Plato Philosophus), etc.:—;Pass., τοὺς νόμους τεταμιεύμεθα we have the laws dealt out , (Lysias Orator):—;Mid., ταμιεύεσθαι εἰς ὅσον βουλόμεθα ἄρχειν to control the limits to which we mean to extend our sway, (Thucydides) 4. of keeping house, to regulate, manage , (Aristophanes Comicus):—; Pass., χώρα ταμιευομένα τινί governed or possessed by one, (Pindar) 5. to store up , (Demosthenes Orator); Ζηνὸς ταμιεύεσκε γονάς she was the depository of it, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

τανυω.definition: 1. to stretch, strain, stretch out , (Iliad by Homer); τ. βιόν to string a bow, (Odyssey by Homer); and in Mid., τόξον τανυσσάμενος having strung his bow, (Iliad by Homer):—;of putting the strings to a harp, ἐτάνυσσε χορδήν (Odyssey by Homer); τ. κανόνα to push the weaving-bar tight , i. e. to weave, (Iliad by Homer); ὅπως τανύσηι when he reins in [the horses, 8th/7th c.BC ]; ἐπὶ Ἀκράγαντι τανύσσας (i.e. ὀϊστούς) having aimed them, (Pindar):—;Pass., γναθμοὶ τάνυσθεν (for ἐτανύσθησαν) the hollow cheeks filled out , (Odyssey by Homer); to run at full stretch , of horses galloping, (Homer) 2. metaphorically to strain, make more intense , μάχην (Iliad by Homer); ἔριδα πολέμοιο πεῖραρ τάνυσσαν strained the tug of war, (Iliad by Homer) 3. to stretch out, lay along, lay , (Homer); τ. τινὰ ἐν κονίηις, ἐπὶ γαίηι to lay one in the dust, stretch him at his length , (Homer):—;Pass. to lie stretched out , (Homer): to extend , (Odyssey by Homer); ἐπὶ χθονὶ κεῖτο τανυσθείς (Iliad by Homer):—;also, τρίβος τετάνυστο the path stretched away , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

ταπεινοφρων.definition: ταπεινόφρων , -ον (ταπεινός, φρήν), [in LXX: (רוּחַ שָׁפָל)* ;] humble-minded : (in bad sense, Plut., 2, 336 E, cf. Deiss., LAE , 72.3).† (AS)

ταραχωδης.definition: 1. troublous, turbulent , (Herdotus Historicus); ἴχνη τ. uncertain, baffling , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. troubled, disordered , (Aristotle Philosopher) 3. of an army, (Thucydides) 4. adverb , ταραχωδῶς ζῆν to live in a state of confusion , (Isocrates Orator); τ. ἔχειν πρός τινα to be rebelliously disposed, (Demosthenes Orator); Sup. -έστατα (Isocrates Orator) (ML)

ταρταρος.definition: Tartarus , a dark abyss, as deep below Hades as earth below heaven, the prison of the Titans, (Iliad by Homer), etc.:—;later, the nether world , like Ἅιδης, (Hesiod) derivation uncertain (ML)

ταφρος.definition: a ditch, trench , (Homer), etc.; τάφρον ὀρύσσειν (Iliad by Homer), etc.; τ. ἐλαύνειν to draw a trench , (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

ταχυνω.definition: 1. to make quickly , (Sophocles Tragicus); τοῖα σπερχόμενος ταχύνει such are the words which in his eager haste he speaks, (Euripides) 2. intransitive to be quick, to make haste, speed, hurry , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

τεινω.definition: 1. to stretch by main force, to stretch to the uttermost , τόξον ἔτεινεν stretched it to its full , (Iliad by Homer); ἐξ ἄντυγος ἡνία τείνας having tied the reins tight to the chariot-rail, (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass., [ ἱμὰς] τέτατο the strap was made tight , (Iliad by Homer); ἱστία τέτατο the sails were stretched , (Odyssey by Homer):—; absolute , μὴ τείνειν ἄγαν not to strain the cord too tight, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. metaphorically , ἶσον τείνειν πολέμου τέλος to strain the even tug of war, (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass., ἐπὶ ἶσα μάχη τέτατο (Iliad by Homer); ἵπποισι τάθη δρόμος their pace was strained to the utmost , (Iliad by Homer): also, to exert oneself, be anxious , (Pindar) 3. to stretch out, spread , Ζεὺς λαίλαπα τείνει (Iliad by Homer); νὺξ τέταται βροτοῖσιν night is spread over mankind, (Odyssey by Homer); so, of light, τέτατο φάος (Sophocles Tragicus); of sound, ἀμφὶ νῶτ᾽ ἐτάθη πάταγος (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. to aim at, direct towards a point, properly from the bow, τείνειν βέλη (Sophocles Tragicus): then, metaphorically , τ. φόνον εἴς τινα to aim death to one, design it for him, (Euripides); τ. λόγον εἴς τινα (Plato Philosophus) 5. to stretch out in length , (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass. to lie out at length, lie stretched , ταθεὶς ἐπὶ γαίηι (Iliad by Homer); ταθεὶς ἐνὶ δεσμῶι lying stretched in chains, (Odyssey by Homer) 6. to stretch or hold out, present , τινὰ ἐπὶ σφαγάν (Euripides):—;Mid., τείνεσθαι χέρε to stretch out one's hands, etc., (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 7. to extend, lengthen , of Time, (Aeschulus Tragicus); τείνειν λόγον (Aeschulus Tragicus) 8. intransitive , of geographical position, to stretch out or extend , (Herdotus Historicus):—;of Time, τείνοντα χρόνον lengthening time, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 9. to exert oneself, struggle , ἐναντία τινί (Plato Philosophus): to hurry on, hasten , (Euripides) 10. to extend to, reach , Lat. pertinere , ἐπὶ τὴν ψυχήν (Plato Philosophus) 11. to tend, refer, belong to , Lat. spectare ad , τείνει ἐς σέ it refers to, concerns you, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; ποῖ τείνε; to what tends it? (Plato Philosophus); ἐγγύς τι τείνειν τοῦ θανάτου (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

τειχηρης.definition: enclosed by walls, beleaguered, besieged , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. (ML)

τειχιζω.definition: 1. to build a wall , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.: with accusative cognate , τ. τεῖχος to build it, (Thucydides); so in Mid., τεῖχος ἐτειχίσσαντο they built them a wall, (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass. to be built , (Pindar): 3rd singular pluperfect τετείχιστο, impersonal , buildings had been erected, there were buildings , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. transitive to wall or fortify , τὸ οὖρος (Herdotus Historicus); τὴν πόλιν (Thucydides): in Mid., τειχίζεσθαι τὸ χωρίον (Thucydides):—;Pass. to be walled or fenced with walls , (Thucydides); τὰ τετειχισμένα the fortified parts , (Thucydides) (ML)

τεκνοποιεω.definition: in Act., of the woman, to bear children , in Mid., of the man, to beget them , (Xenophon Historicus): in Mid. of both parents, to breed children , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

τεκταινομαι.definition: 1. of a carpenter, to make, work, frame , (Iliad by Homer):—; absolute to do joiners' work , opposite to smiths' work, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. of other artificers, (Homeric Hymns) 3. metaphorically to devise, plan, contrive , especially by craft, Lat. machinari , ἐτεκτήναντ᾽ ἀπόφθεγκτόν μ᾽ they kept me from speech of them, (Euripides); πᾶν ἐπ᾽ ἐμοὶ τεκταινέσθω (sc. Cleon) (Aristophanes Comicus) 4. later, Act. τεκταίνω, in same sense, [ variant dates Anthology Palantina , (Lucian); hence participle passive τεκταινόμενος, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

τεκτονικος.definition: practised or skilled in building , (Plato Philosophus): as Substantive a good carpenter or builder , opposite to a smith, (Xenophon Historicus): —; ἡ -κή (i.e. τέχνη); joiners' work, carpentry , (Plato Philosophus), etc. (ML)

τελαμων.definition: 1. a broad strap for bearing anything from Root ! τλα, * τλάω, whence also the hero Telamon took his name, compare Ἄτλας 2. a leathern strap or belt , for bearing both shield or sword, (Homer) 3. a broad linen bandage for wounds, (Iliad by Homer); for swathing mummies, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

τελετη.definition: 1. initiation in the mysteries, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; ἐς χεῖρας ἄγεσθαι τὴν τελετήν to take in hand the matter of initiation , (Herdotus Historicus):—;in plural mystic rites at initiation , (Euripides), etc. 2. a festival accompanied by such rites , in plural , (Pindar); in singular , (Euripides) (ML)

τελευταιος.definition: 1. last , Lat. ultimus , (Herdotus Historicus); τὰ τ. the endings or terminations , (Herdotus Historicus); τελευταίους στῆσαι to station in the rear ranks , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. of Time, ἡ τελευταία, with or without ἡμέρα, the last day allowed for payment, (Demosthenes Orator); one's last day , (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. last, uttermost , ὕβρις (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. τὸ τελευταῖον, as adverb the last time, last of all , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; or τελευταῖον (Plato Philosophus), etc.; and τὰ τελευταῖα (Thucydides) 5. at last, in the last place , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.: but, 6. the adjective is often used with Verbs, where we should use the adverb , ὁ τελευταῖος δραμών (Aeschulus Tragicus); παρελθόντες τελευταῖοι (Thucydides) (ML)

τεμενος.definition: 1. a piece of land cut off, assigned as a domain to kings and chiefs, (Homer) 2. a piece of land dedicated to a god, the sacred precincts , (Homer): in it stood the temple, (Herdotus Historicus):—; metaphorically , the sacred valley of the Nile is the τέμ. Νείλοιο, (Pindar); the Acropolis is the ἱερὸν τ. of Pallas, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

τεμνω.definition: 1. to cut, hew , (Homer), etc.; ὀδόντας οἵους τέμνειν teeth fit for cutting , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. to cut, wound, maim , (Iliad by Homer); πρὸς δέρην τ. to wound her in the neck, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. of a surgeon, to cut , (Iliad by Homer): absolute to use the knife , as opposite to cautery ( κάειν), (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.:—;Pass. to be operated upon , (Plato Philosophus) 4. to cut up, cut to pieces , (Homer), etc.:—; to slaughter, sacrifice , (Iliad by Homer) 5. ὅρκια τάμνειν to sacrifice in attestation of an oath, and so to take solemn oaths , (Homer); θάνατόν νύ τοι ὅρκι᾽ ἔταμνον I made a truce which was death to thee, (Iliad by Homer):—;Mid., of two parties, ὅρκια τάμνεσθαι (Herdotus Historicus):—;cf. Lat. foedus ferire . 6. φάρμακον τέμνειν to cut or chop up a plant for purposes of medicine or witchcraft, (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.; ἄκος τέμνειν to contrive a means or remedy, (Euripides) 7. to divide , of a river, μέσην τ. Λιβύην to cut it in twain, (Herdotus Historicus); δίχα τ. to cut in two, bisect , (Plato Philosophus) 8. to cut asunder, cut off, sever , κεφαλὴν ἀπὸ δειρῆς (Iliad by Homer), etc.; with double accusative , ἐρινεὸν τάμνε ὄρπηκας cut the branches off the fig-tree, (Iliad by Homer); and in Pass., τρίχας ἐτμήθην had them cut off , (Euripides) 9. to part off, mark off , τέμενος (Iliad by Homer) 10. to cut down, fell trees, (Iliad by Homer), etc.:—;Mid., δοῦρα τάμνεσθαι to fell oneself timber, (Odyssey by Homer) 11. λίθον τ. to hew stone, (Plato Philosophus): Mid., λίθους τάμνεσθαι to have them wrought or hewn , (Herdotus Historicus) 12. to cut down for purposes of destruction, (Euripides), etc.; τ. τὴν γῆν to ravage the country by felling the trees and cutting the corn , (Herdotus Historicus); with partitive genitive , τῆς γῆς τ. to waste part of it, (Thucydides) 13. to cut or hew into shape , δούρατα (Odyssey by Homer), etc. 14. to cut lengthwise, to plough , Solon. 15. τ. ὁδόν to cut or make a road, (Thucydides):—;Pass., τέτμηνται κέλευθοι (Pindar) 16. also to make one's way, advance , τ. ὁδόν (Euripides); τὴν μεσόγαιαν τ. τῆς ὁδοῦ to take the middle road, strike through the interior, (Herdotus Historicus); μέσον τέμνειν to hold a middle course, (Plato Philosophus) 17. of ships, to cut through the waves, plough the sea , (Odyssey by Homer):—;so of birds, to cleave the air, (Aristophanes Comicus) 18. to bring to a decision , Lat. decidere , (Pindar) (ML)

τερετρον.definition: a borer, gimlet , Lat. terebra , (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

τερπνος.definition: 1. delightsome, delightful, pleasant, agreeable, glad , (Theognis Elegiacus), etc.; τὸ τερπνόν delight, pleasure , (Thucydides); τὰ τερπνά delights, pleasures , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. of persons, αὑτῷ τερπνός with joy to himself, (Sophocles Tragicus):—; comparative and Sup. τερπνότερος, -ότατος, (Theognis Elegiacus); later, -ιστος:—; adverb τερπνῶς, (Theognis Elegiacus) (ML)

τερπω.definition: 1. to satisfy, delight, gladden, cheer , (Homer), attic:—; absolute to give delight , (Odyssey by Homer); τὰ τέρποντα delights , (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. Pass. and Mid., 3. with genitive rei, to have full enjoyment of a thing, have enough of it, (Homer); metaphorically , τεταρπώμεσθα γόοιο let us take our fill of lamentation, (Homer) 4. to enjoy oneself, make merry , with dative modi, φόρμιγγι, μύθοισι, etc., (Homer), etc.; so, τ. ἐν θαλίῃς (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—; also with participle , τέρψει κλύων (Sophocles Tragicus); τέρπεται τιμώμενος (Euripides):—; absolute , πῖνε καὶ τέρπου drink and be merry , (Herdotus Historicus) 5. with accusative cognate to enjoy , τ. ὄνησιν (Euripides) (ML)

τερψις.definition: enjoyment, delight , τινός from or in a thing, (Hesiod):—; absolute gladness, joy, delight, pleasure , (Theognis Elegiacus) (ML)

τεσσαρακοστος.definition: 1. fortieth , Lat. quadragesimus , (Thucydides) 2. τεσσαρακοστή [ μοῖρα], a fortieth , a coin of Chios, (Thucydides) (ML)

τεσσαρεσκαιδεκα.definition: fourteen , Lat. quatuordecim , the first part remaining unaltered with a neut. Substantive , as, τεσσερεσκαίδεκα ἔτη (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

τετραινω.definition: to bore through, pierce, perforate , (Homer):—;Pass., λίθος τετρημένος (Herdotus Historicus); ὁ οὐρανὸς τέτρηται the sky has holes in it , (Herdotus Historicus); χάσμα τῆς γῆς τετρημένον a chasm formed by perforating the earth, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

τετρακισμυριοι.definition: four times ten thousand, forty thousand , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

τετρας.definition: the fourth day of the month, (Hesiod) (ML)

τεχναζω.definition: 1. to employ art , (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. to use art or cunning, deal subtly, use shifts or subterfuges , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.;—;with infinitive to contrive cunningly that , (Aristotle Philosopher): so aor1 middle ἐτεχνασάμην, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

τηλαυγης.definition: 1. far-shining, far-beaming , (Homeric Hymns) 2. of distant objects, far-seen, conspicuous , (Theognis Elegiacus) 3. adverb -γῶς, clearly, distinctly , (New Testament) (ML)

τιαρα.definition: a tiara , the Persian head-dress, (Herdotus Historicus); worn by the great king, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

τιθηνος.definition: nursing , πόνων τιθηνοὺς ἀποδιδοῦσά σοι τροφάς repaying thee nursing tendance for nursing labours, (Euripides) (ML)

τιμημα.definition: 1. an estimate, valuation , (Euripides) 2. an estimate of damages, a penalty , Lat. litis aestimatio , (Aristophanes Comicus):—;generally a payment , τύμβου for neglect of his tomb, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. estimate of property for taxation, rateable property , Lat. census , (Plato Philosophus), etc.; ἡ ἀπὸ τιμημάτων πολιτεία, = τιμοκρατία, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

τιταν.definition: the Titans , a race of gods placed beneath Tartarus, (Iliad by Homer) (where two are named—;Iapetus and Cronus), accusative to (Hesiod), six sons and six daughters of Uranus and Gaia; hurled from Olympus into nether darkness, (Hesiod): other names are given by later Poets, as Atlas, (Aeschulus Tragicus); Prometheus, (Sophocles Tragicus); Θέμις (Aeschulus Tragicus); and in Lat. Poets Titan is the Sun-god. The oldest derivation of the name is given in (Hesiod), the stretchers, strivers; others connect it with τίτας (from τίνω); avengers. (ML)

τιτρωσκω.definition: 1. to wound , (Homer):—;Pass., τετρῶσθαι τὸν μηρόν to have a wound in the thigh, (Herdotus Historicus): —;with accusative cognate , τιτρώσκειν φόνον to inflict a death wound , (Euripides) 2. generally, to damage, cripple , of ships, (Herdotus Historicus) 3. metaphorically , of wine, to do one a mischief , (Euripides) (ML)

τμητος.definition: 1. cut, shaped by cutting , (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. that can be cut or severed , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

τολμα.definition: 1. courage, to undertake or venture a thing, boldness, daring, hardihood, courage , (Pindar), attic; τῶνδε τόλμαν σχεθεῖν to have courage for this business, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. in bad sense, over-boldness, recklessness , Lat. audacia , [ variant dates Tragica Adespota , etc. 3. a bold or daring act , [ variant dates Tragica Adespota (ML)

τολυπη.definition: a clew or ball of wool , Lat. glomus , [ 5th/4th c.BC , variant dates Anthology Palantina derivation uncertain (ML)

τομη.definition: 1. the end left after cutting, the stump of a tree, (Iliad by Homer); δοκοῦ τ. the end of a beam, (Thucydides); λίθοι ἐν τομῇ ἐγγώνιοι stones cut square, (Thucydides); so, τομῇ προσθεῖσα βόστρυχον having fitted the lock to the place from which it was cut , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. a cutting, hewing, cleaving , ἐν τομᾷ σιδήρου by stroke of iron, (Sophocles Tragicus); φασγάνου τομαί (Euripides):—;as a surgical operation, τομῇ χρῆσθαι (Plato Philosophus); διὰ καύσεών τε καὶ τομῶν by cautery and the knife , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

τοξευμα.definition: 1. that which is shot, an arrow , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; ὅσον τ. ἐξικνέεται the distance of a bowshot , (Herdotus Historicus); πρὶν τ. ἐξικνεῖσθαι before an arrow reached them, (Xenophon Historicus); ἐντὸς τοξεύματος within bow-shot , (Xenophon Historicus); ἔξω τοξεύματος (Thucydides):—; metaphorically , καρδίας τοξεύματα (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. collective in plural for οἱ τοξόται, the archery , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

τοξευω.definition: 1. to shoot with the bow , τινός at a mark, (Iliad by Homer); εἴς τινα (Herdotus Historicus):—; metaphorically to aim at , with genitive , (Euripides):—; absolute to use the bow , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; καθ᾽ ὑπερβολὰν τοξεύσας having shot too high, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. with accusative to shoot or hit with an arrow , τινά (Euripides):—;Pass. to be struck by an arrow , (Thucydides) 3. with accusative rei, to shoot from a bow : metaphorically , to discharge, send forth , ὕμνους (Pindar); ταῦτα ἐτόξευσεν μάτην hath shot these arrows in vain, (Euripides): —;Pass., πᾶν τετόξευται βέλος (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

τοξοτης.definition: 1. a bowman, archer , (Iliad by Homer) 3. at Athens, οἱ τοξόται were the city-guard , also called Σκύθαι, because they were slaves bought from the parts north of Greece, (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. (ML)

τορευτος.definition: worked in relief : metaphorically elaborate , [ variant dates Anthology Palantina from τορεύω (ML)

τραγελαφος.definition: the goat-stag , as the Greeks called a fantastic animal, represented on Eastern carpets and the like, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

τρεπω.definition: 1. to turn or direct towards a thing, (Homer), etc.; mostly followed by a preposition , τρ. τινὰ εἰς εὐνήν to shew him to bed, (Odyssey by Homer); τρ. πόλεις ἐς ὕβριν (Thucydides); τρ. κεφαλὴν πρὸς ἠέλιον (Odyssey by Homer) 2. Pass. to turn one's steps, turn in a certain direction , τραφθῆναι ἀν᾽ Ἑλλάδα to roam up and down Greece, (Odyssey by Homer); with accusative cognate , τρέπεσθαι ὁδόν to take a course, (Herdotus Historicus) 3. Pass. also to turn or betake oneself , εἰς ἀοιδήν (Odyssey by Homer); ἐπὶ ἔργα (Iliad by Homer); ἐφ᾽ ἁρπαγήν (Thucydides); πρὸς ληιστείαν (Thucydides) 4. Pass. and Mid., of places, to be turned or look in a certain direction, πρὸς ζόφον (Odyssey by Homer); πρὸς ἄρκτον, πρὸς νότον (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 5. to turn , i. e. turn about , τρέπειν ἵππους (Iliad by Homer); τὰ καλὰ τρ. ἔζω to turn the best side outmost, (Pindar):—;Pass., αἰχμὴ τράπετο the point bent back , (Iliad by Homer); of the solstice, ἐπειδὰν ἐν χειμῶνι τράπηται ἥλιος (see. τροπή I) (Xenophon Historicus) 6. τρ. τὴν αἰτίαν, τὴν ὀργὴν εἴς τινα to divert the blame, the anger upon another, (Isaeus Orator):—;Pass., in imprecations, ἐς κεφαλὴν τρέποιτο ἐμοί on my head be it! (Aristophanes Comicus) 7. to turn another way, to alter, change , νόον, φρένας (Homer), etc.; ἐς γέλων τρ. τὸ πρᾶγμα (Aristophanes Comicus):—;Pass. to be changed, change , (Homer), etc.; with accusative cognate , τρεπόμενος τροπάς undergoing changes, (Aeschines Orator) 8. to turn or put to flight, rout, defeat , (Iliad by Homer), etc.; τρ. φύγαδε, Lat. convertere in fugam , (Iliad by Homer); τρ. ἐς φυγήν (Euripides);—;so, in aor1 middle , to put an enemy to flight , (Xenophon Historicus):—;Pass. to be put to flight, turn and flee , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.; so in Mid., ἐς φυγὴν τραπέσθαι (Herdotus Historicus):—;also intransitive in Act., φύγαδ᾽ ἔτραπε (Iliad by Homer) 9. to turn away, keep off, hinder , τρ. τινὰ ἀπὸ τείχεος (Iliad by Homer); βέλος ἔτραπεν ἄλληι (Iliad by Homer) 10. to overturn , like ἀνατρέπω, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 11. to turn, apply , τρ. τι ἐς ἄλλο τι (Herdotus Historicus); ποῦ τέτροφας τὰς ἐμβάδα; what have you made of your shoes? (Aristophanes Comicus):—;Pass., ποῖ τρέπεται τὰ χρήματ; (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

τριακονταετης.definition: 1. thirty years old , (Plato Philosophus); in contracted form, οἱ τριακοντοῦται the men of thirty years , (Plato Philosophus); feminine τριακοντοῦτις (Isaeus Orator) 2. τριακονταέτης, ες, of or for thirty years , (Thucydides);—;in feminine form, σπονδαὶ τριηκοντουτίδες (Herdotus Historicus); αἱ τριακοντούτιδες σπονδαί (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

τριακοστος.definition: 1. the thirtieth , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 2. τριακοστή, a duty of one-thirtieth , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

τριβω.definition: 1. to rub: to rub or thresh corn, (Iliad by Homer); μοχλὸν τρῖψαι ἐν ὀφθαλμῶι to work round the stake in his eye, (Odyssey by Homer); χρυσὸν βασάνωι τρ. to rub it on a touchstone, so as to test its purity (compare παρατρίβω), (Theognis Elegiacus):—;Mid., χρηστηρίοις ἐν τοῖσδε τρίβεσθαι μύσος to rub one's pollution upon these shrines, pollute them with it, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. to rub down, grind, pound , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. 3. to crush , βότρυν (Aristophanes Comicus) 4. to wear out by rubbing : Pass., of a road, to wear or tread it smooth , ἀτραπὸς τετριμμένη (Aristophanes Comicus) 5. of Time, to wear away, spend , Lat. terere vitam , (Sophocles Tragicus):—; absolute to waste time, tarry , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 6. to waste or ravage a country, (Euripides) 7. metaphorically , 8. of persons, to wear out , (Hesiod): Pass. to be worn out , (Iliad by Homer):—;Mid., τρίψεσθαι αὐτὴν περὶ αὑτήν to wear itself out by internal struggles, (Thucydides):—;Pass., τριβόμενος ληός an oppressed people, (Herdotus Historicus) 9. of money and property, to waste, squander it, (Herdotus Historicus) 10. to use constantly , (Aristophanes Comicus) 11. Pass. to be much busied or engrossed with a thing, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

τριετης.definition: of or for three years , (Herdotus Historicus): netut. τριέτες as adverb for three years , (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

τριοδους.definition: with three teeth, three-pronged : as Substantive , a trident , (Pindar) (ML)

τρισκαιδεκατος.definition: thirteenth , (Homer), etc.; ἡ τρισκαιδεκάτη (i.e. ἡμέρα); the 13 th day , (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

τρισσος.definition: 1. threefold , Lat. triplex , (Euripides), etc.:—; adverb -ῶς, [ variant dates Anthology Palantina 2. in plural , = τρεῖς, (Pindar), etc. (ML)

τριταιος.definition: 1. on the third day , used with Verbs so as to agree with the subject, τριταῖοι ἐγένοντο ἐν τῇ Ἀττικῇ (Herdotus Historicus); ἐσβεβληκὼς τριταῖος ἐς Μηλιέας having invaded Melis three days before , (Herdotus Historicus); τρ. γενόμενος after being three days dead, (Herdotus Historicus):—; τριταῖος (i.e. πυρετός); a tertian fever , (Plato Philosophus) 2. of events, lasting three days , (Euripides) 3. generally for τρίτος, (Euripides) (ML)

τριχωμα.definition: a growth of hair, hair , (Herdotus Historicus); ἐν γενείου συλλογῇ τριχώματος, i. e. just at the age of manhood, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

τριωροφος.definition: of three stories or floors , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

τροποω.definition: to furnish the oar with its thong : Mid., τροποῦτο κώπην ἀμφὶ σκαλμόν fastened his oar by its thong round the thole, (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;Pass., of the oar, to be furnished with its thong , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

τροφοφορεω.definition: τροφο-φορέω , -ῶ, [in LXX: (נָשָׂא), * ;] to nourish (Hesych.), bear like a nurse (R, mg., bare he them as a nursing-father): with accusative of person(s), , T, Tr., R, mg. (WH, R, txt., τροποφορέω, which see).† (AS)

τρυγητος.definition: 1. a vintage, harvest , (Plutarch) 2. the time thereof, the harvest or vintage , (Thucydides) (ML)

τρυπαω.definition: 1. to bore, pierce through , (Odyssey by Homer):—;Pass., τὰ ὦτα τετρυπημένος having one's ears pierced for earrings , (Xenophon Historicus); ψῆφος τετρυπημένη the pebble of condemnation which had a hole in it , (Aeschines Orator) 2. τρ. τῷ ποδὶ τὴν βελόνην to force the point through the foot, [ variant dates Anthology Palantina (ML)

τρυφερος.definition: 1. delicate, dainty , (Euripides), etc.:—; τὸ τρυφερόν effeminacy , ἐς τὸ τρυφερώτερον to more effeminate habits , (Thucydides):—; neuter as adverb , τρυφερόν voluptuously , (Aristophanes Comicus); τρ. λαλεῖν to speak softly , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

τρωγλη.definition: a hole formed by gnawing, a mouse's hole , (Batrachomyomachia) (ML)

τυλοω.definition: 1. to make knobby :—;Pass., ῥόπαλα σιδήρῳ τετυλωμένα clubs knobbed with iron, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. to make callous , (Xenophon Historicus):—;Pass. to be callous , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

τυμπανον.definition: 1. a kettledrum , such as was used especially in the worship of Cybele, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. a drum-stick : generally, a staff, cudgel , (Aristophanes Comicus) 3. in Virgil tympana are wheels of solid wood. (ML)

τυραννις.definition: 1. kingly power, sovereignty , (Pindar), attic; τ. ὑμῶν lordship over you, (Demosthenes Orator) 3. plural , αἱ τυραννίδες, = οἱ τύραννοι, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

τυχη.definition: 1. the good which man obtains τυγχάνει); by the favour of the gods, good fortune, luck, success , (Theognis Elegiacus), etc.; σὺν τύχῃ (Sophocles Tragicus); θείᾳ τύχῃ, Lat. divinitus , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—; hence Τύχη was deified, like Lat. Fortuna , Τύχη Σώτειρα (Pindar); T. Σωτήρ (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. generally, fortune, chance , good or bad, in singular and plural , (Herdotus Historicus), attic 3. rarely of positive ill fortune , ἢν χρήσωνται τύχῃ, i. e. if they are killed, (Euripides); τύχῃ by ill-luck , (Antipho Orator) 4. especially, ἀγαθὴ τ. (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.; in dative ἀγαθῇ τύχῃ "in God's name, " (Demosthenes Orator), etc.; by crasis, τύχἀγαθῇ (Aristophanes Comicus);—;this formula was also introduced into treaties, like Lat. quod felix faustumque sit , Λάχης εἶπε, τύχῃ ἀγαθῇ τῶν Ἀθηναίων ποιεῖσθαι τὴν ἐκεχειρίαν Decret. in (Thucydides):—;so ἐπ᾽ ἀγαθῇ τύχῃ (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. 5. Adverbial usages, τύχῃ by chance , Lat. forte , forte fortuna, (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.; ἀπὸ τύχης (Aristotle Philosopher); ἐκ τύχης (Plato Philosophus); διὰ τύχην (Isocrates Orator), etc.; κατὰ τύχην (Thucydides), etc. 6. a chance, hap, accident , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.; τῆς τύχης, τὸ ἐμὲ τυχεῖν . . ! what a piece of ill-luck , that . . ! (Xenophon Historicus); mostly of mishaps, misfortunes , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc. (ML)

υαινα.definition: the hyaena , an animal of the dog kind, with a bristly mane like a hog (whence the name), (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

υβριστικος.definition: given to wantonness, wanton, insolent, outrageous , (Plato Philosophus), etc.:—; τὸ ὑβριστικόν an insolent disposition , (Xenophon Historicus):—; adverb -κῶς, (Plato Philosophus); comparative -ώτερον, (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

υγιεια.definition: 1. health, soundness of body, Lat. salus , (Herdotus Historicus), attic:—; plural ὑγίειαι, healthy states or conditions , (Plato Philosophus) 2. of the mind, ὑ. φρενῶν soundness of mind, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

υγραινω.definition: to wet, moisten , (Euripides): of a river, to water a country, (Euripides) (ML)

υδρευω.definition: to draw, fetch or carry water , (Odyssey by Homer):—;Mid. to draw water for oneself, fetch water , πολῖται (Odyssey by Homer), attic (ML)

υδροφορος.definition: 1. carrying water , (Plutarch) 2. as Substantive , ὑδρ., a water-carrier , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

υειος.definition: of or belonging to swine , ὑεία κοιλία pig's tripe, (Aristophanes Comicus):—; θηρίον ὕ., as a type of brutish ignorance, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

υλακτεω.definition: 1. to bark, bay, howl , of dogs, (Iliad by Homer); of hounds, to give tongue , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. metaphorically , κραδίη ὑλακτεῖ howls for rage , (Odyssey by Homer); with accusative cognate to yell forth bold and shameless words , (Sophocles Tragicus); ἄμους᾽ ὑλακτῶν howling his uncouth songs, (Euripides) 3. transitive to bark at , τινά (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

υλωδης.definition: 1. woody, wooded , (Thucydides); τὰ ὑλώδη wooded ground , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. turbid, muddy , (Plutarch) (ML)

υμνωδεω.definition: 1. to sing a hymn or song of praise : generally, to sing , ὑμν. θρῆνον (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. = χρησμῳδέω, (Euripides)[ ῦ in (Aeschulus Tragicus)] (ML)

υπαιθρος.definition: 1. as Substantive , ἐν ὑπαίθρῳ, entry Dio, in the open air , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. τὰ ὕπαιθρα, the field, the open country , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

υπατος.definition: 1. like Lat. summus for supremus, the highest, uppermost , of Zeus, ὕπατος κρειόντων, θεῶν ὕπ., (Homer); οἱ ὕπατοι the gods above , Lat. superi , opposite to οἱ χθόνιοι, Lat. inferi , (Aeschulus Tragicus); ὕπατός τις some god above , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. simply of Place, ἐν πυρῇ ὑπάτῃ on the very top of the funeral pile, (Iliad by Homer) 3. of Time, last , Lat. supremus , (Sophocles Tragicus) 5. with genitive , like the preposition ὑπό, ὕπατος χώρας supreme over the land, (Aeschulus Tragicus); ὕπατοι λεχέων high above the nest, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 6. as Substantive , ὕπατος, the Roman consul , (Polybius Historicus), etc. (ML)

υπερειζω.definition: to set up, prop up, support

υπερηφανεω.definition: 1. much like ὑπερηνορέων overweening, arrogant , (Iliad by Homer) 2. transitive to treat disdainfully , (Lucian) (ML)

υπερκειμαι.definition: 1. Dep. 2. to lie or be situate above , (Isocrates Orator) 3. to be postponed , (Lucian) (ML)

υπερμηκης.definition: 1. exceeding long , (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἡ βασιλέος χεὶρ ὑπ. the king's arm is very long, reaches very far , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. exceeding high , of mountains, (Herdotus Historicus) 3. ὑπερμάκης βοά a cry exceeding loud , (Pindar) (ML)

υπεροραω.definition: ὑπερ-οράω , see: ὑπερεῖδον. ὑπερ-εῖδον , aor. [in LXX for עָלַם hi., מַעַל, etc. ;] to overlook : with accusative of thing(s), (AS)

υπερτιθημι.definition: 1. to set higher, erect , [ variant dates Anthology Palantina 2. to set on the other side, carry over , (Plutarch) 3. in Mid. to hold over , so as to protect, [ variant dates Anthology Palantina 4. metaphorically , παντὶ θεὸν ὑπερτιθέμεν to set God over all, (Pindar) 5. to communicate a thing to another, ὑπερετίθεα (ionic imperfect for -ετίθην); τὰ ἔμελλον ποιήσειν (Herdotus Historicus):—;so in Mid., especially in order to ask advice, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

υπερφερω.definition: 1. to bear or carry over a place, ὑπ. τὸν ἰσθμὸν τὰς ναῦς (Thucydides):—;Pass., [ αἱ ναῦς] αἱ ὑπερενεχθεῖσαι τὸν ἰσθμόν (Thucydides) 2. intransitive to rise above, to surpass, excel, have the advantage over , τινός τινι one in a thing, (Herdotus Historicus); also with accusative pro genitive , ὑπερφέρεις τόλμῃ τόλμαν (Euripides): absolute to excel, have preeminence , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

υπευθυνος.definition: 1. liable to give account for one's administration of an office, accountable, responsible , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—; ὑπεύθυνοι, οἱ, at Athens, magistrates who had to submit their accounts to public auditors λογισταί); (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. 2. with genitive responsible for , ὑπ. ἀρχῆς ἑτέρας quoted in (Demosthenes Orator); of slaves, σῶμα ὑπ. ἀδικημάτων their body is liable for their misdeeds, i. e. they must pay for them with their body, (Demosthenes Orator) 3. with dative responsible to another, dependent on them, Lat. obnoxius , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

υπηρεσια.definition: 1. the body of rowers and sailors, the ship's crew , (Thucydides), etc. 2. service , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. (ML)

υπνοω.definition: to put to sleep :—; Pass. to fall asleep, sleep , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

υποβλεπω.definition: to look up from under the brows at, glance at, to look askance at, eye suspiciously or angrily , Lat. limis oculis suspicere , (Plato Philosophus); also ὑπ. ἐλεεινά to cast piteous glances , [ variant dates Anthology Palantina :—;Pass. to be looked at with suspicion , (Euripides) (ML)

υποδυτης.definition: a garment under a coat of mail , (Plutarch) (ML)

υποκαιω.definition: 1. to burn by applying fire below , (Herdotus Historicus): to offer secret sacrifices , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. to light under , (Lucian) (ML)

υποκειμαι.definition: 1. to lie under or beneath , (Iliad by Homer); with dative , (Plato Philosophus) 2. in various metaphorically senses, 3. to be put under the eyes or mind, i. e. to be submitted or proposed to one , (Pindar); αἱ ὑποκείμεναι ἐλπίδες one's present hopes, (Demosthenes Orator); ὑπόκειταί μοι ὅτι . . I have laid down the rule , that . ., (Herdotus Historicus) 4. to be laid down or assumed as an hypothesis , (Plato Philosophus), etc.; τούτων ὑποκειμένων = Lat. his positis , (Plato Philosophus); impersonal , ὑπόκειται a rule is laid down , (Demosthenes Orator); ὑποκείσθω ὅτι . . let it be granted that . ., (Aristotle Philosopher) 5. to be suggested , (Herdotus Historicus) 6. to be left at bottom, left remaining , (Thucydides) 7. to be subject to, submit to , τινι (Plato Philosophus): absolute to be submissive , (Plato Philosophus) 8. to be left behind in pledge, to be pledged or mortgaged , τινος for a certain sum, (Demosthenes Orator), etc.; ὑποκείμενοι, of persons, bound for payment of a sum of money, (Demosthenes Orator) 9. to underlie , as a substratum, (Plato Philosophus), etc. 10. to be subordinate , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

υπολειμμα.definition: ὑπό-λειμμα (WH, -λιμμα, see their App. , 154), -τος, τό, [in LXX chiefly for שָׁאַר ;] a remnant : (Arist., al.; cf. κατάλειμμα).† (AS)

υπολοιπος.definition: 1. left behind, staying behind , (Herdotus Historicus); οἱ ὑπ. those who remained alive , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. of things, ὑπ. τὸ βάραθρον γίγνεται the pit still remains , (Aristophanes Comicus); ὅσα ἦν ὑπ. all that remained to be done , (Thucydides) (ML)

υπολυω.definition: 1. to loosen beneath or below , ὑπέλυσε γυῖα made his limbs give way under him , (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass., γυῖα ὑπέλυντο (Iliad by Homer) 2. to loose from under the yoke, (Homer):—; to loose from bonds , (Odyssey by Homer); in Mid., τὸν ὑπελύσαο δεσμῶν thou didst free him from bonds by stealth , (Iliad by Homer) 3. to untie a person's sandals from under his feet, take off his shoes, (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;Mid. to take off one's sandals or shoes, or to have them taken off , (Aristophanes Comicus) 4. with accusative pers. to unshoe him, take off his shoes , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

υπομνημα.definition: 1. a remembrance, memorial , (Thucydides), etc. 2. a note, memorandum , (Demosthenes Orator):—;in plural memoranda, notes, minutes , Lat. commentarii , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

υπονυσσω.definition: to prick or sting underneath : generally, to sting , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

υποπιπτω.definition: 1. to fall under or down, to sink in , (Plutarch) 2. to fall down before any one, with accusative , (Plato Philosophus): —;hence, to be subject to him, fall under his power, (Isocrates Orator); of a flatterer, to cringe to , τινί (Demosthenes Orator); with accusative ὑποπεσὼν τὸν δεσπότην (Aristophanes Comicus) 3. to fall behind another, (Demosthenes Orator) 4. to get in under or among , (Thucydides) 5. of accidents, to happen, fall out , (Isocrates Orator) 6. of persons, to fall under a punishment, with dative , (Plutarch) 7. of places, to lie under or below , with dative , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

υποπτευω.definition: 1. to be suspicious , (Xenophon Historicus); also, ὑπ. εἴς τινα to have suspicions of him, (Thucydides) 2. to suspect, guess, suppose , (Xenophon Historicus) 3. transitive to suspect, hold in suspicion , (Sophocles Tragicus); ὑπ. τινὰ εἴς τι of something, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;Pass. to be suspected, mistrusted , (Thucydides); impersonal , ὡς ὑπωπτεύετο as was generally suspected , (Xenophon Historicus) 4. with accusative pers. et infinitive to suspect that , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 5. with accusative rei, to look suspiciously on , (Thucydides):—;but also, ὑπ. τι to suspect something, (Euripides) from ὑπόπτης (ML)

υποσκελιζω.definition: 1. to trip up one's heels, upset , Lat. supplantare , (Demosthenes Orator) 2. metaphorically , ὑπ. καὶ ἀνατρέπων (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

υπουργος.definition: rendering service, serviceable, promoting, conducive to a thing, with dative , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

υποφαυσις.definition: a light shewing through a small hole: a narrow opening , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

υποχειριος.definition: 1. under the hand, in hand , (Odyssey by Homer) 2. of persons, under any one's hand, under command, subject , τινι (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; λαβεῖν τινα ὑποχείριον to get into one's power , (Euripides); ἔχειν τινὰ ὑπ. (Thucydides) (ML)

υποχρεως.definition: 1. indebted, in debt , (Aristophanes Comicus); ὑπ. τινος his debtor , (Plutarch) 2. of property, involved , Lat. obaeratus , (Demosthenes Orator) 3. with genitive , ὑπ. φιλίας bound by ties of friendship, (Plutarch) (ML)

υπτιαζω.gloss: to turn up and open hands
υπτιαζω.definition: to bend oneself back, to carry one's head high , (Aeschines Orator):—;Pass., κάρα ὑπτιάζεται his head lies supine , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

υπτιος.definition: 1. laid back, laid on one's back , πέσεν ὕπτιος he fell backwards , opposite to πρηνής, (Iliad by Homer); of a quadruped, ὀρθοῦ ἑστεῶτος καὶ ὑπτίου rearing upright and falling backwards , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. generally with the under side uppermost , χείρ ὑπτία the hollow of the hand, (Plutarch); ἐξ ὑπτίου κράνους from the upturned helmet, with the hollow uppermost , (Aeschulus Tragicus); so, παράθες ὑπτίαν τὴν ἀσπίδα); (Aristophanes Comicus); ἀψὶς ὑπτία a half-wheel with the concave side uppermost , (Herdotus Historicus); ὑπτίοις σέλμασιν ναυτίλλεται he sails with the bottom uppermost , i. e. suffers shipwreck, (Sophocles Tragicus); ἐξ ὑπτίας νεῖν to swim on the back (in metaphorically sense), (Plato Philosophus) 3. of land, sloping evenly , of Egypt, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

υφαινω.definition: 1. to weave , ἱστὸν ὑφαίνειν to weave a web, (Homer); ἱμάτιον (Plato Philosophus), etc.:—; absolute to weave, ply the loom , (Herdotus Historicus):—;Mid., ἱμάτιον ὑφαίνεσθαι to weave oneself a cloak, (Plato Philosophus) 2. to contrive, plan, invent , Lat. texere , δόλον ὑφαίνειν (Iliad by Homer); μῆτιν ὑφ. (Odyssey by Homer) 3. generally, to create, construct , (Pindar) (ML)

υφαιρεω.definition: 1. to seize underneath or inwardly , (Homer) 2. to draw or take away from under a thing, with genitive , (Iliad by Homer):—;also τὴν χεῖρα ὑφῄρει tried to draw it away , (Aristophanes Comicus) 3. to take away underhand, filch away , (Thucydides); ὑφ. τῆς ὑποψίας gradually to take away part of . ., (Thucydides):—;Pass., ὑπαραιρημένος (ionic perfect participle ) put secretly away, made away with , (Herdotus Historicus):—;so in Mid. to take away underhand, filch away, purloin , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 4. in Mid. also with accusative pers., ὑφ. τινά τινος to rob him of a thing, (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

υφιστημι.definition: 1. in these tenses Causal, to place or set under , τί τινι (Herdotus Historicus); τρεῖς σταυροὺς ὑπίστησι plants three piles in the lake to support a house, (Herdotus Historicus):—; metaphorically , γνώμας ὑποστήσας σοφάς having laid them as a foundation , (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. to post secretly or in ambush , (Herdotus Historicus) 3. Causal also in future and aor1 middle to substitute , τί τινι one thing for another, (Xenophon Historicus) 4. Pass., with aorist2 active ὑπ-έστην, perfect ὑφ-έστηκα, ionic participle ὑπ-εστεώς:—; to stand under as a support , with dative , (Herdotus Historicus) 5. to sink to the bottom, settle , τὸ ὑφιστάμενον the milk, opposite to τὸ ἐφιστάμενον (the cream), (Herdotus Historicus) 6. to place oneself under an engagement, engage or promise to do, with infinitive future , ὅσς᾽ Ἀχιλῆι ὑπέστημεν δώσειν (Iliad by Homer), etc.; with infinitive aorist , οὔ τίς με ὑπέστη σαῶσαι (Iliad by Homer); with infinitive present , (Herdotus Historicus):—; absolute , after promise given , (Odyssey by Homer); ὥσπερ ὑπέστη as he promised , (Thucydides):—;when followed by accusative , an infinitive may be supplied, τρίποδας οὕς οἱ ὑπέστη (i.e. δώσειν); (Iliad by Homer); ἐκτελέουσιν ὑπόσχεσιν ἥνπερ ὑπέσταν (Iliad by Homer) 7. to submit to any one, τινι (Iliad by Homer) 8. with accusative rei, to submit to, consent to , ὁ τὸ ἐλάχιστον ὑπιστάμενος who offers to take the least, (Herdotus Historicus); ὑφ. τὸν πλοῦν to undertake it unwillingly , (Thucydides); so, ὑφ. τὸν κίνδυνον (Thucydides): —;rarely with dative , ὑφ. ξυμφοραῖς ταῖς μεγίσταις (Thucydides) 9. to undertake an office, (Xenophon Historicus) 10. to lie concealed or in ambush , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 11. to support an attack, to resist, withstand , with dative , (Aeschulus Tragicus); with accusative , (Euripides):—; absolute to stand one's ground, face the enemy , Lat. subsistere , (Euripides) (ML)

υω.definition: 1. to send rain, to rain , Ζεὺς ὗε (Homer), etc.; ὁ θεὸς ὕει (Herdotus Historicus):—;then, the nom. being omitted, ὕει used impersonal , Lat. pluit , it rains, (Hesiod); ὕοντος when it is raining , (Aristophanes Comicus); ὕοντος πολλῷ as it was raining heavily, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. with accusative loci, ἑπτὰ ἐτέων οὐκ ὗε τὴν Θήρην for seven years it did not rain on Thera, (Herdotus Historicus):—;hence in Pass., with future middle to be rained on , (Odyssey by Homer); ὕσθησαν αἱ Θῆβαι Thebes was rained upon , i. e. it rained there, (Herdotus Historicus); ἡ χώρη ὕεται, i. e. it rains in the country, (Herdotus Historicus) 3. with accusative cognate , ὗσε χρυσόν it rained gold, (Pindar); καινὸν ἀεὶ Ζεὺς ὕει ὕδωρ (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

φαιος.definition: dusky, dun, gray , Lat. fuscus , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

φακος.definition: lentil , and its fruit , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. (ML)

φαλακρος.definition: baldheaded, bald , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; πρόσωπον φαλακρόν (Euripides) (ML)

φαρετρα.definition: a quiver for arrows, Lat. pharetra , (Homer) (ML)

φαρμακευω.definition: 1. to administer a drug , (Plato Philosophus) 2. to use enchantments , φαρμακεύειν τι ἐς τὸν ποταμόν to use it as a charm to calm the river, (Herdotus Historicus) 3. with accusative pers. to drug, give him a poisonous or stupefying drug , (Euripides) (ML)

φαρμακον.definition: φάρμακον , -ου, τό, [in LXX for כֶּשֶׁף ;] __(a) a drug ; __(b) an in­cantation, enchantment : , Tr., mg., WH, txt. (RV, sorceries).† (AS)

φαρυγξ.definition: the throat, gullet , (Odyssey by Homer), etc. (ML)

φασμα.definition: 1. an apparition, phantom , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; φ. ἀνδρός the spectral appearance of a man, (Herdotus Historicus):—; a vision in a dream, (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc. 2. a sign from heaven, portent, omen , (Herdotus Historicus); periphrastic , φάσμα ταύρου a monster of a bull, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

φαυλιζω.definition: to hold cheap, to depreciate, disparage , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

φερνη.definition: that which is brought by the wife (compare ἕδνον); a dowry, portion , Lat. dos , (Herdotus Historicus); also in plural of a dower , as consisting of divers presents, (Euripides); but, φερναὶ πολέμου, of a wife won in battle, (Euripides):—;in plural , also, bridal gifts , (Euripides) (ML)

φθεγμα.definition: 1. the sound of the voice, a voice , (Pindar), etc.: of a person, ὦ φθέγμ᾽ ἀναιδές, for ὦ φθεγξάμενε ἀναιδῆ, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. language, speech , (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. a saying, word , (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. of other sounds, as of birds, cries , (Sophocles Tragicus); of a bull, roaring , (Euripides); φθ. θυείας the grinding of the mortar, (Aristophanes Comicus); of the nightingale's song, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

φιλογεωργος.definition: fond of a country life , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

φιλονεικεω.definition: 1. to be fond of strife, engage in eager rivalry, be contentious , φιλονεικῶν out of contentiousness or party spirit , (Thucydides); φ. πρός τινα (Lysias Orator):—;with accusative , φ. τὸ ἐμὲ εἶναι τὸν ἀποκρινόμενον to be eager that I should be the answerer, (Plato Philosophus); τὰ χείρω φ. to be so obstinate as to choose the worst, (Thucydides) 2. in good sense, to struggle emulously , φ. περὶ τῶν καλλίστων (Isocrates Orator) (ML)

φιμος.definition: 1. a muzzle , Lat. capistrum , (Lucian) 2. the nose-band of a horse's bridle, fitted with pipes through which the horses' breath made a whistling sound, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. a kind of cup , used as a dice-box , Lat. fritillus , (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

φλεγμαινω.definition: to be heated, inflamed, to fester , φλεγμαίνουσα πόλις, opposite to ὑγιής, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

φλεγω.definition: 1. transitive to burn, burn up , (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass. to take fire, blaze up , (Iliad by Homer) 2. metaphorically to kindle, inflame with passion, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Pass., like Lat. uri , to burn with passion, be inflamed, (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. to light up , Ζεὺς βέλος φλέγων making it blaze or flash , (Aeschulus Tragicus); metaphorically , ἄταν οὐρανίαν φλέγων letting the flame of mischief blaze up to heaven, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Pass. to blaze up, be a-light , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 4. metaphorically to make illustrious or famous , Lat. illustrare , (Pindar):—;Pass. to be or become so , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 5. intransitive to burn, flame, blaze , (Aeschulus Tragicus); of armour, to flash , (Euripides) 6. metaphorically to break forth , of passion, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 7. to shine forth, become famous , (Pindar) (ML)

φλεψ.definition: 1. a vein , (Iliad by Homer), etc.; φλέβα σχάζειν to open a vein , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. a vein of metal, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

φλια.definition: in plural φλιαί, = σταθμοί, the doorposts, jambs , (Odyssey by Homer); in singular , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

φοινικεος.definition: purple-red, purple or crimson , and (generally) red , Lat. puniceus , (Herdotus Historicus):—;attic contracted φοινι-κοῦς, ᾶ, οῦν, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

φρικη.definition: 1. a shuddering, shivering , (Plato Philosophus) 2. shuddering , especially from religious awe, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

φρικωδης.definition: that causes shuddering, horrible , (Euripides):—; neuter φρικῶδες, as adverb horribly , (Euripides):—; adverb -δῶς, Sup., φρικωδέστατα ἔχειν to be in utter horror , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

φροντις.definition: 1. thought, care, heed, attention bestowed upon a person or thing, with genitive , φροντίδ᾽ ἔχειν τινός (Euripides); ἐν φροντίδι εἶναι περί τινος (Herdotus Historicus) 2. absolute thought, meditation , (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἐν φροντίδι μοι ἐγένετο [ τὸ πρῆγμα] (Herdotus Historicus); ἐμβῆσαί τινα ἐς φροντίδα to set one a thinking , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;in plural thoughts , αἱ δεύτεραί πως φροντίδες σοφώτεραι (Euripides) 3. deep thought, care, concern , (Aeschulus Tragicus); οὐ φροντὶς Ἱπποκλείδῃ no matter to Hippocleides! (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

φρουρα.definition: 1. a looking out, watch, guard , as a duty, (Herdotus Historicus); φρουρὰν ἄζηλον ὀχήσω shall keep unenviable watch , (Aeschulus Tragicus); φρουρὰ ὄμματος my watchful eye, (Sophocles Tragicus); φρουρᾶς ᾄδειν to sing while on guard , (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. a prison , (Plato Philosophus) 3. of persons, a watch, guard, garrison , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; especially of frontier-posts , which were guarded in Attica by the περίπολοι, (Xenophon Historicus) 4. at Sparta, a body of men destined for service , φρουρὰν φαίνειν (see. φαίνω A. 1. 5). (ML)

φρυαγμα.definition: 1. a violent snorting, neighing , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. metaphorically wanton behaviour, insolence , [ variant dates Anthology Palantina (ML)

φρυγω.definition: 1. to roast or fry , (Aristophanes Comicus); ἐρετμοῖσι φρύξουσι they shall cook with the [wood of] the oars, (Oracle quoted in Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass., πεφρυγμέναι κριθαί roasted barley, (Thucydides) 2. of the sun, to parch , Lat. torrere , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

φυγαδευω.definition: to drive from a country, banish , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

φυγας.definition: 1. one who flees from his country, a runaway, fugitive, a banished man, exile, refugee , Lat. exul, profugus , (Herdotus Historicus), attic; φυγάδα ποιεῖν τινα (Xenophon Historicus); κατάγειν φυγάδας to recall them; etc. 2. of an army, put to flight , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

φυη.definition: 1. growth, stature , especially fine growth, noble stature , (Homer); Νέστορι εἶδός τε μέγεθός τε φυήν τt ἄγχιστα ἐῴκει he was like Nestor both in shape and size and stature (or growth) , (Iliad by Homer) 2. poetry for φύσις, one's natural powers, nature, genius , (Pindar) 3. the flower or prime of age , (Pindar) (ML)

φυλαρχος.definition: 1. the chief of a φυ_λή, a phylarch , (Herdotus Historicus):—;used to translated the Rom. tribunus , (Plutarch) 2. at Athens, the commander of the cavalry furnished by each tribe , see. ἵππαρχος. (ML)

φυραω.definition: 1. to mix flour or meal so as to make it into dough, to knead , (Herdotus Historicus); γῆν φυράσειν φόνῳ to make earth into a bloody paste , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;Pass., οἴνῳ καὶ ἐλαίῳ πεφυραμένα ἄλφιτα (Thucydides) 2. metaphorically , μαλακὴν φωνὴν φυράσασθαι to make up a soft voice, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

φυρω.definition: 1. to mix something dry with something wet , mostly with a sense of mixing so as to soil or defile , δάκρυσιν εἵματ᾽ ἔφυρον they wetted, sullied their garments with tears, (Iliad by Homer); also with genitive , χείλεα φύρσω αἵματος (Odyssey by Homer):—;Pass., δάκρυσι πεφυρμένη (Iliad by Homer); αἵματι οἶκος ἐφύρθη (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. of dry things, κόνει φύρουσα κάρα (Euripides); γαίαι πεφύρσεσθαι κόμαν to be doomed to have one's hair defiled with earth, (Pindar) 3. metaphorically to mingle together, confuse , ἔφυρον εἰκῆ πάντα they mixed all things up together, did all at random, (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.:—;Pass. to be mixed up , ἐκ πεφυρμένου καὶ θηριώδους from a confused and savage state, (Euripides) 4. in Pass. also to mix with others, have dealings with him, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

φυσαω.definition: 1. transitive to puff or blow up, distend , (Aristophanes Comicus); of bag-pipers, (Aristophanes Comicus); φ. τὰς γνάθους to puff them out , (Demosthenes Orator):—;Pass. to be inflated , ἡ γαστὴρ ἐπεφύσητό μοι (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. metaphorically to puff one up, make him vain , and so to cheat , (Demosthenes Orator):—;Pass. to be puffed up , ἐπί τινι at a thing, (Xenophon Historicus) 3. to blow up, kindle a fire: but also 4. to blow out, extinguish , τὴν λαμπάδα (Aristophanes Comicus) 5. to blow out, spurt out , (Sophocles Tragicus) 6. to blow a wind-instrument, (Euripides) (ML)
