φυσητηρ.definition: an instrument for blowing, blowpipe or tube , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

φυτον.definition: 1. that which has grown, a plant, tree , (Iliad by Homer), etc. 2. generally a creature , of men, (Euripides) 3. like ἔρνος, of men, a descendant, child , (Euripides) (ML)

φωραω.definition: 1. to search after a thief or theft, search a house , (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. in Pass. to be detected , (Demosthenes Orator); with participle , κλέπτης ὢν φωρᾶσθαι (Demosthenes Orator); so, κακὸς [ ὢν] ἐφωράθη φίλοις (Euripides):—;also of things, ἀργύριον ἐφωράθη ἐξαγόμενον money was discovered to be in course of exportation, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

χαλιξ.definition: 1. a small stone, pebble , in plural , (Lucian), etc. 2. as collect. in singular , gravel, rubble , used in building, (Thucydides); so also in plural , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

χαλκειον.definition: 1. a smith's shop, forge, smithy , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. = χαλκίον, a copper, caldron , (Herdotus Historicus) 3. a metal reflector in a lamp, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

χαλκειος.definition: of copper or bronze, brasen , (Homer); χαλκήιος δόμος, = χαλκεῖον, a forge , (Odyssey by Homer); χάλκειον γένος, of the Age of brass , (Hesiod) (ML)

χαλκευω.definition: 1. to make of copper or (generally) of metal, to forge , (Iliad by Homer), etc.:—;Mid. to forge for oneself , (Theognis Elegiacus):—;Pass. to be wrought or forged , (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. absolute to be a smith, work as a smith, ply the hammer , (Aristophanes Comicus); τὸ χαλκεύειν the smith's art , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

χαμαιλεων.definition: the chameleon , a kind of lizard known for changing its colour, (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

χαος.definition: 1. chaos , the first stateof the universe, (Hesiod), etc. 2. infinite space, the expanse , (Aristophanes Comicus) 3. the nether abyss, infinite darkness , [ variant dates Anthology Palantina (ML)

χαραδριος.definition: perhaps a yellowish bird dwelling in clefts the curlew , (Aristophanes Comicus): χαραδριοῦ βίον ζῆν, of a glutton, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

χαρακοω.definition: to fence by a palisade, fortify , (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

χαρασσω.definition: 1. to make sharp or pointed, sharpen, whet , (Hesiod) 2. to furnish with notches or teeth , like a saw, (Aristotle Philosopher):—;Pass., σκύταλον κεχ. ὄζοις a staff jagged or rugged with branches, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus): metaphorically , [ ὄμμα] ἠλεμάτοις ἀκτῖσι χαράσσεται sparkles with false lights, of the effect produced by painting the eye-lids, [ variant dates Anthology Palantina 3. metaphorically in Pass., κεχαραγμένος τινί exasperated at any one, (Herdotus Historicus); κείνῳ τόδε μὴ χαράσσου be not angry at him for this, (Euripides) 4. to cut into furrows, cut, scratch , (Pindar):—;Pass., κέκοπται καὶ χαράσσεται πέδον (Aeschulus Tragicus) 5. to engrave, inscribe , [ Refs 3rd c.BC , variant dates Anthology Palantina (ML)

χαρμονη.definition: 1. a joy , (Euripides); plural joys, delights , (Euripides) 2. = χάρμα II, joy, delight , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

χειμερινος.definition: 1. of or in winter, of or in winter-time , opposite to θερινός, χ. τροπαί (see. τροπή 1), (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; τὴν χ. (i.e. ὥρην); during the winter season , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. wintry , (Thucydides); see. χειμέριος. (ML)

χειροτονια.definition: 1. a voting or electing by show of hands , (Thucydides) 2. a vote , Lat. suffragium , in plural , (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

χειροω.definition: 1. to bring into hand, to manage, master, subdue , (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. mostly in Mid., to conquer, overpower, subdue , (Herdotus Historicus); so, τήνδ᾽ ἐχειρούμην ἄγραν became master of this booty, (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. without any sense of violence, to master, subdue , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. 4. χειροῦμαι is also Pass. to be subdued , [ variant dates Tragica Adespota ; future χειρωθήσομαι (Demosthenes Orator); aor1 ἐχειρώθην (Herdotus Historicus); perfect κεχείρωμαι (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

χελιδων.definition: 1. the swallow , (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—; the twittering of the swallow was proverbially used of barbarous tongues by the Greeks, (Aeschulus Tragicus); χελιδόνων μουσεῖα (see. μουσεῖον); proverbs also, μία χελιδὼν ἔαρ οὐ ποιεῖ (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. the frog in a horse's foot , so called from its being forked like the swallow's tail , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

χελωνη.definition: 1. a tortoise , (Homeric Hymns); prov. of insensibility, ἰὼ χελῶναι μακάριαι τοῦ δέρματος oh ye tortoises , happy in your thick skins! (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. like Roman testudo, a pent-house formed of shields overlapping each other like the scales on a tortoise's back , used by storming parties in approaching a city's walls: then, generally, a pent-house for protecting besiegers, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

χερσαιος.definition: on or of dry land , ὄρνιθες χ. land- birds, opposite to λιμναῖοι, (Herdotus Historicus); χ. κροκόδειλος a lizard, (Herdotus Historicus):—;also of landsmen , as opposite to seamen, (Euripides); κῦμα χερσαῖον στρατοῦ, an army, opposite to a fleet, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

χερσος.definition: 1. dry land, land , ἐπὶ χέρσου, opposite to ἐν πόντῳ, (Odyssey by Homer); κύματα κυλινδόμενα προτὶ χέρσον (Odyssey by Homer); κῦμα χέρσῳ ῥηγνύμενον (Iliad by Homer); χέρσῳ on or by land , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. as adjective , χέρσος, ον, dry, firm , of land, (Herdotus Historicus); ἐν κονίᾳ χέρσῳ, opposite to πόντῳ, (Pindar) 3. dry, hard, barren , (Herdotus Historicus); χ. λιμήν a harbour left dry , [ variant dates Anthology Palantina 4. metaphorically barren, without children , of women, (Sophocles Tragicus): with genitive barren of , πυρὰ χέρσος ἀγλαϊσμάτων (Euripides) Prob. from same Root as ξηρός. (ML)

χεω.definition: 1. Radic. sense, to pour : 2. properly of liquids, to pour out, pour , (Homer), etc.; Zeus χέει ὕδωρ, i. e. he makes it rain, (Iliad by Homer); χέει χιόνα βορέας (Euripides); absolute , χέει it snows , (Iliad by Homer):—;Mid. to pour for oneself , especially of drink-offerings, χοὰς χεόμην νεκύεσσι (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—;Pass., χέονται κρῆναι they gush forth , (Euripides); χυθέντος ποτοῦ ἐς γῆν (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. χ. δάκρυα to shed tears, (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass., of tears, to pour or gush forth , (Homer); so of blood, to be shed , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 4. in Pass. to become liquid, melt, thaw , (Xenophon Historicus) 5. of solids, to shed, scatter , φύλλα (Iliad by Homer); πτερά (Odyssey by Homer); χ. κόνιν κὰκ κεφαλῆς (Homer); χ. καλάμην χθονί, of a mower or reaper (see. καλάμη), (Iliad by Homer) 6. like χώννυμι, to throw out earth, so as to form a mound, σῆμα, τύμβον χ. (Homer) 7. χ. δοῦρα to pour or shower spears, (Iliad by Homer); Mid., βέλεα χέοντο they showered their arrows, (Iliad by Homer) 8. to let fall or drop , ἡνία (Iliad by Homer); so, χέειν κρόκου βαφὰς (see. βαφή II) (Aeschulus Tragicus); but, καρπὸν χ., of trees, to produce fruit abundantly , (Odyssey by Homer) 9. in Pass. to be thrown or heaped up together , (Homer) 10. in Pass. also of living beings, to pour or stream in a dense mass or throng , (Homer) 11. metaphorically of sounds, to pour forth , φωνήν, αὐδήν (Odyssey by Homer); φθόγγον (Aeschulus Tragicus) 12. of things that obscure the sight, κατ᾽ ὀφθαλμῶν χέεν ἀχλύν shed a dark cloud over the eyes, (Iliad by Homer); πολλὴν ἠέρα χεῦε shed a mist abroad, (Odyssey by Homer):—;Pass., ἀμφὶ δέ οἱ θάνατος χύτο was shed around him, (Iliad by Homer); νόσος κέχυται (Sophocles Tragicus); φρὶξ ἐπὶ πόντον ἐχεύατο (Mid. in passive sense), (Iliad by Homer) 13. of persons, ἀμφ᾽ αὐτῶι χυμένη throwing herself around him, (Homer): so in Mid., ἀμφὶ υἱὸν ἐχεύατο πήχεε (Iliad by Homer) 14. perfect passive κέχυμαι, to be wholly engaged in , Δᾶλος, ἐν ἇι κέχυμαι (Pindar) (ML)

χηλη.definition: 1. a horse's hoof , (Hesiod):—;also, a cloven hoof , (Euripides) 2. in plural , of the talons of a bird, [ variant dates Tragica Adespota ; of a wolf's claws , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 3. a sea-bank, breakwater , formed of stones laid at the base of a sea-wall, to break the force of the waves (so called because it projected like a hoof) , Lat. crepido , (Thucydides) 4. the spur of a mountain or ridge of rocks answering a like purpose, (Thucydides) 5. a cloven implement , such as a netting-needle;—; compare χηλεύω. (ML)

χηρευω.definition: 1. intransitive to be bereaved of a person or thing, with genitive , (Odyssey by Homer) 2. absolute to be bereaved of a husband, to be widowed, live in widowhood , (Demosthenes Orator), etc.;—;of a man, to be a widower , (Plutarch); so, χηρεύσει λέχος (Euripides) 3. to live in solitude , of an exile, (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. transitive to bereave , (Euripides) (ML)

χθιζος.definition: of yesterday , τὸ χθιζὸν χρεῖος their yesterday's debt, (Iliad by Homer); ὁ χθ. πόνος yesterday's labour, (Herdotus Historicus); in adverbial sense, with Verbs, χθιζὸς ἔβη he went yesterday , (Iliad by Homer); χθ. ἤλυθες (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—; neuter χθιζόν as adverb = χθές, (Homer); so plural χθιζά, see. πρώιζος. (ML)

χθων.definition: 1. the earth, ground , (Homer); χθόνα δῦναι to go beneath the earth , i. e. to die, (Iliad by Homer); κατὰ χθονὸς κρύπτειν τινά (Sophocles Tragicus); κούφα σοι χθὼν ἐπάνω πέσοι (Euripides) 2. of the nether world , οἱ ὑπὸ χθονός, i. e. those in the shades below , Lat. inferi , (Aeschulus Tragicus); κατὰ χθονὸς θεαί, i. e. the Erinyes, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. earth , i. e. the whole earth, the world , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 4. Earth , as a goddess, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 5. a particular land or country , of Ithaca, (Odyssey by Homer); of Libya, (Pindar); χθὼν Ἀσιᾶτις, Δωρίς, Ἀργεία, Ἑλλάς, Ἰδαία, etc., [ variant dates Tragica Adespota (ML)

χιδρον.definition: unripe wheaten groats , as ἄλφιτα are barley-groats, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

χιλιαρχια.definition: 1. the office or post of χιλίαρχος, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. the office of the tribuni militares , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

χιμαιρα.definition: 1. a she-goat , Lat. capra , (Iliad by Homer), attic 2. Χίμαιρα, ἡ, Chimaera , a firespouting-monster, with lion's head, serpent's tail, and goat's body, killed by Bellerophon, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

χιμαρος.definition: 1. a he-goat , Lat. caper , = τράγος, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. also feminine = χίμαιρα, [ Refs 3rd c.BC , variant dates Anthology Palantina (ML)

χλαινα.definition: Lat. laena , a large square upper-garment, a cloak, mantle, (Homer); it was made of wool, and worn over the χιτών, thrown over the shoulders, fastened with a pin or brooch περόνη). It is also called φᾶρος by (Homer), and in later Greek ἱμάτιον, Latin pallium. derivation uncertain (ML)

χνοος.definition: 1. any light porous substance , ἁλὸς χνόος the foam that gathers at the edge of the sea, (Odyssey by Homer); πωλικὸς χν. horse's foam , [ variant dates Anthology Palantina 2. the first down on the chin of youths, Lat. lanugo , (Aristophanes Comicus): the bloom on fruit, [ variant dates Anthology Palantina (ML)

χολος.definition: 1. like χόλη, gall, bile , (Iliad by Homer) 2. generally metaphorically bile, gall, bitter anger, wrath , (Homer), attic; χόλος ἔδυ τινά (Iliad by Homer); χόλος ἔμπεσε θυμῷ (Iliad by Homer); χόλον πέσσειν, καταπέσσειν (see. entry); χ. σβέσσαι παῦσαι (Iliad by Homer); χόλου παύεσθαι (Hesiod):—;with genitive objecti, anger towards or because of another, (Iliad by Homer); with genitive rei, anger for, because of a thing, (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. an object of anger , [ variant dates Anthology Palantina (ML)

χορδη.definition: 1. gut-string, the string of a lyre, Lat. chorda , (Odyssey by Homer) 2. tripe , (Batrachomyomachia): also = χόρδευμα, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

χορευω.definition: 1. to dance a round or choral dance , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.; especially of the Bacchic chorus, (Euripides):—; to take part in the chorus , regarded as a matter of religion, (Sophocles Tragicus): to be one of a chorus , (Aristophanes Comicus): —;with dative pers. to dance to him, in his honour , (Euripides) 2. generally, to dance , especially from joy, (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. metaphorically to practise a thing, be versed in it, (Plato Philosophus) 4. with accusative cognate , φροίμιον χορεύσομαι I will dance a prelude (to festivities), (Aeschulus Tragicus); χ. γάμους to celebrate them, (Euripides); ὄργια Μουσῶν (Aristophanes Comicus):—;Mid., χορεύεσθαι δίνας to ply the eddying dance , (Euripides):—;Pass., κεχόρευται ἡμῖν (sings the Chorus) our part is played , (Aristophanes Comicus) 5. transitive to celebrate in choral dance , Ἴακχον (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Pass. to be celebrated in choral dance , (Aristophanes Comicus) 6. Causal, to set one a dancing, to rouse, wake to the dance , τινά (Euripides); so, πόδα χορεύειν [ variant dates Anthology Palantina (ML)

χορηγια.definition: 1. the office of a χορηγός at Athens, the defraying of the cost of the public choruses , being the chief of the λειτουργίαι, (Thucydides), etc. 2. means for providing χοροί: abundance of means, fortune , (Aristotle Philosopher) 3. metaphorically supplies for war , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

χοριον.definition: the membrane that encloses the fetus, the afterbirth , Lat. secundae : plural χόρια, ων, τά, a dish made by stuffing it with honey and milk , a kind of haggis , (Aristophanes Comicus): proverbial , χαλεπὸν χορίω (doric genitive ) κύνα γεῦσαι "don't let a dog taste blood, " (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (cf. Horace, canis a corio nunquam absterrebitur uncto). (ML)

χορτασια.definition: a being fed, feasting , [ variant dates Anthology Palantina (ML)

χους.definition: a coos, a measurement of liquid ()

χρεμετιζω.definition: to neigh, whinny , Lat. hinnire , of horses, (Iliad by Homer), etc. Formed from the sound. (ML)

χρεος.definition: 1. that which one needs must pay, an obligation, debt , (Odyssey by Homer); a debt for stolen cattle , (Iliad by Homer); χρεῖος ἀποστήσασθαι to pay a debt in full, (Iliad by Homer); ἀρᾶς τίνει χρ. pays the debt demanded by the curse, (Aeschulus Tragicus); χρέος πόλει προσάπτειν to attach a further debt , i.e. guilt to the city, (Sophocles Tragicus); χρέος ἀποδιδόναι to repay a debt , (Herdotus Historicus):—;in plural debts , χρειῶν λύσις (Hesiod); τὴν οὐσίαν ἅπασαν χρέα κατέλιπε left all the property in outstanding debts , (Demosthenes Orator) 2. a needful business, an affair, matter , ἑὸν αὐτοῦ χρεῖος (Odyssey by Homer): a requirement, a purpose , (Sophocles Tragicus): with genitive , like χάριν, for the sake of , σὸν οὐκ ἔλασσον ἢ κείνης χρέος (Euripides) 3. like χρῆμα, a thing , τί χρέο; = τί χρῆμ; wherefore? (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἐφ᾽ ὅ τι χρ. ἐμόλετ; (Euripides) 4. in (Odyssey by Homer), ἦλθον Τειρεσίαο κατὰ χρέος seems to be = Τειρεσίᾳ χρησόμενος, I came to consult him:—;but, κατὰ χρέος according to what is due , as is meet , (Homeric Hymns) 5. a duty, task, charge, office , (Pindar) (ML)

χρησμολογεω.definition: to utter oracles, divine , (Aristophanes Comicus) from χρησμολόγος (ML)

χροια.definition: 1. the surface of a body, the skin; the body itself, (Iliad by Homer) 2. the superficial appearance of a thing, its colour , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.:—;especially the colour of the skin, the complexion , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

χρυσοχοος.definition: 1. one who melts gold , of one who gilds the horns of a victim, (Odyssey by Homer) 2. a goldsmith , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

χυτος.definition: 1. poured, shed , αἷμα χυτόν blood shed , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. of dry things, shot out, heaped up , χυτὴ γαῖα a mound of earth, a sepulchral mound, (Homer):—;as Substantive , χυτός, οῦ, = χῶμα, a mound, bank, dike , (Herdotus Historicus) 3. melted , ἀρτήματα λίθινα χυτά pendants of melted stone, (Herdotus Historicus) 4. generally, liquid, flowing , [ Refs 5th c.BC , variant dates Anthology Palantina (ML)

χυτρα.definition: 1. an earthen pot, a pot for boiling, pipkin , Lat. olla , (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. χύτραι, pots of pulse offered to inferior deities, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

χυτροπους.definition: a pot with feet , or a portable stove for putting a pot upon, (Hesiod) (ML)

χωλαινω.definition: to be or go lame , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

χωμα.definition: 1. earth thrown up, a bank, mound , thrown up against the walls of cities to take them, (Herdotus Historicus):—; a dike to hinder a river from overflowing, (Herdotus Historicus):—; a dam , (Herdotus Historicus):—; a mole or pier , carried out into the sea, Lat. moles , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. like Lat. tumulus , a sepulchral mound, [ Refs 5th c.BC , variant dates Tragica Adespota (ML)

χωνευω.definition: 1. to cast into a mould ( χόανος), (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. to cast metal: —;Pass., κεχωνευμένος (Plutarch) (ML)

ψαλις.definition: 1. a pair of scissors , Lat. forfex , [ variant dates Anthology Palantina 2. a building with a pointed stone roof, a vault , Lat. fornix , (Sophocles Tragicus) Deriv. unknown. (ML)

ψαλτωδεω.gloss: to sing along with stringed instruments
ψαλτωδεω.definition: to sing along with stringed instruments

ψαρος.definition: like a starling , i. e. speckled, dappled , ψ. ἵππος a dapple-gray horse, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

ψελλιζω.definition: to falter in speech, speak inarticulately :—;so in Mid., (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

ψηφισμα.definition: a proposition carried by vote : especially a measure passed in the ἐκκλησία, a decree , (Aristophanes Comicus); τὸ Μεγαρέων ψ. the decree concerning them, (Thucydides); so, περὶ Μεγαρέων ψ. (Thucydides); ψ. γράφειν to bring in a decree , (Aristophanes Comicus); ψ. ἐπιψηφίζειν, of the πρόεδροι, to put it to the vote, (Aeschines Orator); ψ. νικᾶν to carry it , (Aeschines Orator); ψ. καθαιρεῖν to rescind it , Lat. abrogare , (Thucydides) (ML)

ψιθυριζω.definition: to whisper, say into the ear , (Plato Philosophus):—; metaphorically , ὅταν πλάτανος πτελέᾳ ψιθυρίζῃ when the plane whispers to the elm, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

ψιλος.definition: 1. bare , 2. of land, ψιλὴ ἄροσις a bare corn-field, (Iliad by Homer); πεδίον μέγα τε καὶ ψιλόν (Herdotus Historicus): with genitive , γῆ ψιλὴ δενδρέων land bare of trees, (Herdotus Historicus):—; ψιλὴ γεωργία the tillage of land for corn , opposite to γ. πεφυτευμένη (for vines and olives) , (Aristotle Philosopher) 3. of animals, stript of hair or feathers, bare, smooth , δέρμα (Odyssey by Homer); ἶβις ψιλὴ κεφαλήν bald on the head, (Herdotus Historicus) 4. generally, bare, uncovered , ψιλὸν ὡς ὁρᾷ νέκυν (Sophocles Tragicus):—;with genitive bare of, separated from , ψιλὴ σώματος οὖσα [ ἡ ψυχή] (Plato Philosophus) b. bare, stript of appendages , ψιλὴ τρόπις the bare keel with the planks torn from it, (Odyssey by Homer); ψ. θρίδαξ a lettuce with the side-leaves pulled off , (Herdotus Historicus); ψ. μάχαιραι swords without other arms , (Xenophon Historicus) 5. οἱ ψιλοί (i.e. τῶν ὅπλων); soldiers without heavy armour, light troops , such as archers and slingers, opposite to ὁπλῖται, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; τὸ ψιλόν, opposite to τὸ ὁπλιτικόν, (Xenophon Historicus); ψ. ἔχων τὴν κεφαλήν bare-headed, without helmet , (Xenophon Historicus) 6. ψιλὸς λόγος bare language, i. e. prose , as opposite to poetry which is clothed in metre, (Plato Philosophus); also, ψ. λόγος is a mere speech, a speech unsupported by evidence , (Demosthenes Orator) 7. ψιλὴ ποίησις mere poetry, without music , i. e. epic poetry, as opposite to lyric , (Plato Philosophus):—;but, ψιλὴ μουσική instrumental music unaccompanied by the voice , (Aristotle Philosopher) 8. Oedipus seems to call Antigone his ψιλὸν ὄμμα, as being the one poor eye left him, (Sophocles Tragicus) 9. adverb ψιλῶς, merely, only , (Plutarch) (ML)

ψιλοω.definition: 1. to strip bare of hair, (Herdotus Historicus):—; Pass. to become bald , (Hesiod): generally, to be laid bare , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. with genitive to strip bare of, to strip of a thing, (Herdotus Historicus) 3. generally, to leave naked, unarmed or defenceless , (Thucydides) 4. Pass. also of things, to be stripped off something, τὰ κρέα ἐψιλωμένα τῶν ὀστέων (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

ψογος.definition: 1. a blamable fault, a blemish, flaw , (Simonides Lyricus) 2. blame, censure , (Pindar) (ML)

ψοφεω.definition: 1. to make an inarticulate noise, to sound, make a noise , (Euripides); ψοφεῖ λάλον τι sounds chatter-like , as if it were tested like a pot, to see if it were cracked, (Aristophanes Comicus); ὥσπερ κύμβαλον ψοφεῖ (Xenophon Historicus) 2. with accusative , ψοφεῖν τὰς θύρας to knock at the door inside, to shew that some one was coming out, Menand.:—;also of the door ( intransitive ), εἰ αἱ θύραι νύκτωρ ψοφοῖεν, i. e. if they were heard to open , (Lysias Orator) (ML)

ψοφος.definition: 1. any inarticulate sound, a sound, noise , (Homer), etc.; of musical instruments, ψ. λωτοῦ, κιθάρας (Euripides) 2. a mere sound, empty sound, noise , (Sophocles Tragicus); ψόφου πλέως, of Aeschylus, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

ψυκτηρ.definition: a wine-cooler , a vessel holding from 2 to 6 μετρηταί, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

ψωμος.definition: a morsel, bit , ψωμοὶ ἀνδρόμεοι gobbets of man's flesh, Virgil's sanies ac frusta , (Odyssey by Homer); also in (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

ψωρα.definition: the itch, scurvy, scab, mange , Lat. scabies , impetigo, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

ωθεω.definition: 1. to thrust, push, shove, force onwards or away , λᾶαν ἄνω ὤθεσκε he kept pushing it upwards, (Odyssey by Homer); ἀπ᾽ ὀφθαλμῶν νέφος ὦσεν Ἀθήνη (Iliad by Homer); ἐκ μηροῦ δόρυ ὦσε he forced the spear from the thigh, (Iliad by Homer); ὦσαί τινα ἀφ᾽ ἵππων (Iliad by Homer); ὦσαι ἑαυτὸν ἐς τὸ πῦρ to rush into the fire, (Herdotus Historicus); so, ὠθ. τινὰ ἐπὶ κεφαλήν to throw him headlong down, (Plato Philosophus); κατὰ πετρῶν (Euripides); ὦσαι τὴν θύραν to force the door, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. to push or force back in battle, (Iliad by Homer) 3. to thrust out, banish , [ variant dates Tragica Adespota ; ὦσαί τινα φυγάδα (Plato Philosophus); ὠθ. τινα ἄθαπτον (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. metaphorically , ὠθ. τὰ πρήγματα to push matters on, hurry them, (Herdotus Historicus) 5. absolute , ὦσα παρέξ pushed off from land, (Odyssey by Homer); ὤθει βιαίως (Euripides) 6. Mid., mostly in aor1, to thrust or push from oneself, push or force back, repulse , especially in battle, τείχεος ἂψ ὤσασθαι (Iliad by Homer); ὤσασθαι προτὶ Ἴλιον, προτὶ ἄστυ (Iliad by Homer); ὤσασθαι τὴν ἵππον (Herdotus Historicus); ὠσαμένων τὸ κέρας (Thucydides) 7. Pass. to be thrust on, to fall violently , ἐπὶ κεφαλήν (Herdotus Historicus); πρὸς βίαν (Euripides) 8. to force one's way , (Xenophon Historicus): to crowd on, throng , like ὠστίζομαι, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

ωραιοτης.definition: 1. ripeness of fruits , (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. the bloom of youth , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

ωφελημα.definition: 1. a useful or serviceable thing, a service, benefit , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. generally, use, advantage, profit , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

στρεπτος.definition: 1. flexible, pliant : στρεπτὸς χιτών a shirt of chain-armour , Lat. lorica annulata , (Iliad by Homer); στρεπταὶ λύγοι pliant withs, (Euripides): twined, wreathed , [ variant dates Anthology Palantina 2. στρεπτός, οῦ, a collar of twisted or linked metal , Lat. torques , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 3. of pastry, a twist or roll , (Demosthenes Orator) 4. metaphorically to be bent or turned , στρεπτοὶ καὶ θεοὶ αὐτοί the gods themselves may be turned (by prayer), (Iliad by Homer); στρ. γλῶσσα a glib, pliant tongue, (Iliad by Homer) 5. bent, curved , of a pick-axe, (Euripides); of a bow, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

εικοστος.definition: 1. the twentieth , (Odyssey by Homer); epic also ἐεικοστός, (Iliad by Homer) 2. εἰκοστή, ἡ, a tax of a twentieth , Lat. vicesima , levied by the Athenians on imports and exports from the allies in lieu of tribute, (Thucydides) (ML)

ακι.definition: without exception ( εν ακί at is a transliterration of אֵ֣ין נָקִ֔י)

πηροω.definition: disable, cripple ( - variant א P66 P75)

προβατιον.definition: προβάτιον , -ου, τό, dimin. of πρόβατον (used as a term of endearment, see El., § 27, 4), a little sheep : (πρόβατα, WH, mg.).† (AS)

προσανεχω.definition: προσ-αν-έχω , to approach : seel. for προσαχέω, L.† (AS)

υσσος.definition: ὑσσός , -ο, ό, a javelin (see ref. s.v, ὕσσωπος) (AS)
